## The asset lock

Written **before** anyone starts searching or generating — Step 5b has a pipeline but no
spec upstream of it, and an asset sourced without a spec is an asset chosen by whatever the
search returned. One block per media slot:

```text
Asset role: [hero image / texture / illustration / thumbnail / cutout]
Slot: [dimensions / aspect ratio / location on the page]
Art direction: [source, palette, subject, rendering, crop, density]
Avoid: [wrong palette, extra text, brand drift, generic placeholders]
```

The `Avoid` line is the one that earns its keep: it is the reject field applied to a single
asset, and it is what a QA pass compares the delivered frame against.
*"Generated assets must be placed into the implementation before handoff or documented as
blocked"* — never quietly downgraded to a gradient. That downgrade is the media-role drift
this file's next section already bans, caught one step earlier.

---

## Anti-averaging

Choose a dominant direction. Secondary references contribute narrow, named details;
they do not get to soften the primary one. The failure mode is specific: a dark
workbench reference, an acid-yellow document site, and a serif editorial page do not
average into a warm cream canvas with muted clay accents — **dark + acid + serif is
not cream + orange + polite serif.** Dark → cream, saturated → muted clay, sharp →
rounded, distinctive layout → generic hero-and-sections: each swap is the
intersection eating the direction, not synthesis.

Run these against the lock before shipping — ported from `anti-ai-slop.md`:

- **Identity test.** If the first viewport could belong to any other company,
  branding lost to averaging. Add the one detail that makes this unmistakably *this*
  brand's build.
- **Editorial test.** If swapping the logo for a coffee shop, boutique hotel, or
  literary magazine still makes the hero feel plausible, the build has drifted into
  generic calm-editorial slop regardless of what the lock says on paper.
- **Screenshot test.** Would this pass next to real products in the named
  register, or does it read as the safe middle every other page also landed on?

A lock that names a dominant primary and still fails these three was averaged during
implementation, not during research — check the built page against the lock's
"Reject" line specifically.

## Token-role and media-role preservation

**Token-role preservation.** A source's role for a colour, radius, shadow, or
component is part of the token, not separable from it. A CTA-only accent used as a
section background, a code-only syntax colour promoted to UI chrome, or a decorative
gradient turned into a core surface are all role drift. Preserve the role or drop
the token — never repurpose it to make a layout "work."

**Media-role preservation.** An image-led reference never collapses to text-only
because the image was hard to produce. If the real asset genuinely is not
available, the placeholder must be honest, not silent:

```text
Placeholder — [slot name]
Aspect: [ratio, e.g. 16:9 desktop / 4:3 mobile]
Art direction: [subject, lighting, crop the real asset will match]
Alt: [describes the intended real subject, not "placeholder image"]
```

A placeholder with no aspect ratio, no art direction, and generic alt text is the
same failure as no image at all — it just fails one render cycle later.

---

## Three persona sketches

`SKILL.md` Step 5 pass 12 and [`verbs/review.md`](verbs/review.md) § 4 both resolve ties
with "named personas". Nothing in the chain created any, so the tie-break pointed at an
artifact that did not exist. It does now, and it is three lines in `BRIEF.md` — not the
per-project persona documents upstream files away, which is a research deliverable this
chain has no room for.

Select and write **three**, following upstream's proportions (*"2–3 primary users, 1–2 edge
case users, 1 stress case user"*), compressed to one line each:

```text
Primary: [who they are] · [device and connection] · [what they came to do]
Edge:    [who sits at the margin] · [the ability or context that puts them there] · [what breaks first]
Stress:  [the same job under a named difficult circumstance] · [what they cannot afford to lose]
```

**The conditions are situational, not only permanent.** Upstream's spectrum is explicit that
*"bright sunlight, noisy environment, one hand occupied, driving, multitasking, emotional
distress, unfamiliar language, slow connection"* belong beside vision, hearing, motor and
cognitive conditions. A stress persona on a Swedish harbour-restaurant page is a person on a
phone, outdoors, in sun, deciding where to eat in the next ten minutes — and that persona
decides more layout questions than any abstract one.

**Write the intersections down.** *"A sighted user in bright sunlight has similar needs to a
low-vision user. A stressed parent holding a baby has similar motor constraints to someone
with limited hand mobility. A non-native speaker has similar needs to someone with a
cognitive processing difference."* Each intersection is a universal-design opportunity: one
fix that pays twice.

**Then ask the one question that makes the set honest:** *"Which persona makes you most
uncomfortable?"* — *"that one probably needs the most attention."* Ask it of the brief, and
of the user when there is a user to ask. Discomfort is the signal that a persona was
included for completeness and is about to be designed around rather than for.

Sketches that read as cardboard cutouts have failed. The check is upstream's own: *"do these
feel like real people, or cardboard cutouts?"*

## Feeding Step 2 and Step 5

**Into Step 2.** At **Tier 2**, the lock *is* the direction — its primary reference
sets the token commitments directly. At **Tiers 0–1**, the lock is the **quality
bar** the locked or derived system has to clear: the locked tokens still win on
value, but the captured references are what "as good as" means, concretely.

**Into Step 5 visual QA.** Carry the lock's fields straight into the QA pass:

```text
Source truth: [the reference lock, or the DESIGN.md it fed]
Implementation evidence: [local screenshot, deployed URL screenshot, captured app state]
Viewport/state: [desktop/mobile, route, theme, interaction state]
```

Classify findings P0–P3 (broken/unreadable · major drift from the lock · moderate
mismatch or missing state · post-handoff polish). **No handoff with an open P0, P1,
or P2.** A P3 may ship with the finding named; P0–P2 block.

## Worked example — Skärgårdskrogen (Swedish harbour restaurant, warm photographic)

A harbourside restaurant on the Bohuslän coast. Register: **warm photographic**
(`SKILL.md` register table — harbour restaurant, guesthouse, tourism, family
business), with `klova/` as this skill's own in-repo worked example for the
register (`house-physics.md`).

**Research loop:**

1. Broad aesthetic — "warm coastal Nordic hospitality."
2. Domain/category — harbourside seafood dining, Bohuslän archipelago.
3. Known brand — a west-coast Swedish harbour restaurant with a photograph-led site.
4. Register — warm photographic, per the table above; cross-check against `klova/`.
5. Anti-reference — the editorial-print register (`calyx.html`): its apparatus on a
   family harbour restaurant reads as pretension, not craft.

Four captured and read: `klova/` itself, two competitor harbour-restaurant sites,
and `calyx.html` as the anti-reference boundary check.

**Reference-lock block:**

```text
Primary reference/direction: klova/ — centred logo lockup over full-bleed harbour photography, no rail, no kicker, no edition marker.
Preserve: centred logo lockup with no rail; full-bleed hero photograph with generous framing air on secondary images; one real outlined button sized to be pressed; warm serif display at conversational (not oversized-drop-cap) scale; dark-navy footer as the page's one tonal inversion.
Borrow only: dotted carousel indicator for the food gallery (competitor B — klova/ has no gallery, so this is a genuinely new need, not a style import); 12px rounded image corners (competitor B).
Role rules: the outlined button is CTA-only, never a secondary link style; the navy footer tone is inversion-only, never a section background elsewhere on the page.
Media strategy: photo:unsplash, sourced and vendored per photo-sources.md until real restaurant photography is supplied; hero 16:9 desktop / 4:3 mobile, framed with 24-48px air — never full-bleed-with-type-over, the editorial-print move this build explicitly rejects.
Reject: kicker microformat, grain film, ledger pricing, edition markers, italic serif drop caps — all editorial-print apparatus a family harbour restaurant cannot plausibly publish.
Token commitments: warm ivory canvas; near-black ink; one terracotta accent used only on the button and one wordmark word (never as fill); slate captions with a separate, measured value for the dark footer ground.
```

**Decision ledger:**

| Decision | Source | Source rule/role | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Warm photographic, not editorial print | `SKILL.md` register table + anti-reference read of `calyx.html` | register selects apparatus | Family-run harbour restaurant, not a publishing entity |
| Centred logo lockup, no rail | `klova/` (primary) | layout role: identity-first hero | The photograph is the primary hire, not editorial structure |
| Real outlined button | `klova/` (primary) | CTA-only | Warm-photographic register expects a pressable button, unlike print/cinematic typeset links |
| Dotted carousel for gallery | Competitor B (borrowed) | gallery navigation only | `klova/` had no gallery; licensed as one named borrowed detail, not a wholesale style import |
| One terracotta accent, display-scale only | `house-physics.md` structural rule | accent role: CTA + display, never fill | Prevents the accent diluting into a second colour system |

A rejected direction here would average `klova/`'s warm photographic register with
`calyx.html`'s editorial apparatus into a soft-cream page with a restrained kicker
and a half-outlined button that is neither a typeset link nor a real one — the
dark+acid+serif-vs-cream+orange+polite-serif failure, in miniature.

## Two additions from the 2026-09-03 A/B run (AB05)

- **A colour-swapped word in a headline is a gate-89 signal even without a serif.** "Se *exakt* vad som ändrades" with *exakt* in the accent is the same reflex as the italic word swap; use it only when a locked reference does it and the word carries the claim.
- **Token commitments name the anatomy of every priced or listed surface.** Write `pricing: ledger (hairline rows, display numerals)` or `features: label-rail`, so the lock carries house physics into Step 4 instead of falling back to bordered cards.

   'Work [cards] 24-26'), the product sitting inside the headline (Don Molinico's
   jar in 'Pimientos del piquillo', Assistantly's mascot in the gap of 'with
   Talent'), photos slotted between the lines of the studio's biggest sentence
   (Ashley Brooke CS), creators placed in the gaps of a split statement (Patreon).
   This is what separates a designed page from a stack of text blocks and image
   blocks.
6. **Smoothing is a choice, measured.** Lenis showcase sites travel 40–220 px after
   the wheel stops. Above ~180 px pages read as floaty (Bulbs, SK Archive); the house
   value (`lerp .075`, `wheelMultiplier .6`) sits in the lower half on purpose and is
   not raised to look "smoother".
7. **Gates are for experiences only.** About one in six showcase sites gates entry
   (ENTER, sound on/off, choose a path). A persuade page never gates. An experience
   page may, but the gate is a designed object (Chasing the Moment's ticket that
   tears into the sound choice), and "without sound" is always offered.

## 3. Intro patterns (pick one per page)

| Pattern | What happens | Seen on | Plugins |
|---|---|---|---|
| Counter → mark | A number counts up; its last frame becomes the hero mark | ddark, nickho-motorsports, a24-raviklaassens, khanhnguyen | core, CustomEase |
| Copy first | 2–3 timed lines on black, then the hero is lit | seewhateyesee, forgeautomotive-co | SplitText |
| Curtain / push | A bar wipes or a character shoves the loader off | filmbot, huyml | core |
| Letters out of blur | Name assembles letter by letter from blur or grey | millemannwines, forgeautomotive-co, mattjinn | SplitText, CustomEase |
| Object in the loader | The loader's moving part is the hero object | family-ikea | core + WebGL |
| Scene fade-up | Logo mark on ground, the scene window rises | illoca-unseen, davidecattaneo | SplitText |

## 4. Transition causes (rule 2 vocabulary)

sheet-over · film-stack · card-to-full-bleed grow · ground change through an image ·
pixel-block dissolve · dot-field forms the next object · tool wipe (highlighter) ·
slats/blinds · hinge stand-up · scan bars · panel grows from the axis · bar-built
display words · horizontal pin pan (Khanh) · camera dolly in a 3D scene (Illoca) ·
wheel-cut between full-bleed films (Forms, Jason Bradley) · pixel-cut edge that is
the logo's unit (Huehaus) · diagonal wipe one layer deeper (Hashgraph) · portal
through the hero's own shape (Moblinks) · contents pouring out of a screen (Poly) ·
light change on the ground itself (Daylight) · data swarm reforming (Getty) · two
statements handing over inside one set of line masks (Alunix R9 tes).

## 5. Below the floor (observed, not to copy)

- Virtual scroll with no progress indicator (Millemann, Illoca): the reader cannot
  tell how far they are.
- Giant words permanently cropped at both edges (Cip Harvin) read as fragments.
- Ghost-grey text before activation, below contrast for long stretches (a-lign,
  Forge before the fill).
- Wheel-only content with no scroll path (A24 discs, Huy Phan, Jesper Landberg).
  Fine for an experiment, wrong for a page that must be read.
- A gate on a page whose job is to persuade.

## 6. Measured stack (from `motion/probe.json`)

Measured over **564 read sites** from `motion/probe.json` (`scripts/catalogue/showcase_stats.py`).

| Measure | Sites |
|---|---|
| GSAP loaded | 515 (91 %) |
| GSAP minor versions | 3.12: 146, 3.15: 139, 3.13: 138, 3.14: 75, 3.11: 20, 3.10: 5 |
| Lenis | 415 (74 %) |
| ScrollSmoother | 25 (4 %) |
| Locomotive | 5 (1 %) |
| Pinned sections | 115 (20 %) |
| WebGL canvas | 273 (48 %) |
| Page transitions (Barba / Swup / Taxi) | 55 / 12 / 34 |
| Smoothed scroll | 352 (62 %); px still travelling after the wheel stops: median 154, p25 134, p75 177 |
| Floor 2 / 1 / 0 (lead's reading) | 65 / 304 / 195 |
| Grammar | chaptered editorial: 335, continuous world: 44, gallery/catalog: 43, live surface: 41, filmic one-shot: 39, rhythmic cutlist: 29, typographic poster: 18, split stage: 13, none: 2 |
| Register | cinematic dark: 195, modern clean: 145, other: 62, warm photographic: 58, editorial print: 55, illustrated dark: 41, historical art: 8 |
| Mode | persuade: 328, experience: 124, read: 107, operate: 5 |

What the numbers say for a house page:

- **Lenis is the norm, ScrollSmoother the exception** (74 % against 4 %): the house
  choice (one Lenis, no ScrollSmoother beside it) is the showcase's own default.
- **Pins are a tool, not a style.** One site in five pins anything. The floor-2 pages
  pin one or two acts and let the rest flow; a page that pins every section is not
  on the list.
- **WebGL is half the showcase, but not half of floor 2.** Many floor-2 pages
  (Huehaus, Bohdan, Ashley Brooke CS, Daylight, Hungry Tiger) carry their journey with
  clip-path, masks, photography and type. The journey is the requirement, the
  renderer is not.
- **The house pace sits low in the measured band.** Smoothed pages travel 134–177 px
  after the wheel stops (median 154); the house Lenis (`lerp .075`, `wheelMultiplier
  .6`) is set for a calm read, and is not raised to look "smoother" (rule 6).
- **Chaptered editorial dominates** (333 of 562). The floor is therefore not "become a
  continuous world": it is that a chaptered page still makes every chapter change a
  material event (rule 2) and carries one object through (rule 3).

103	## 3. What makes it a journey (the part to keep)
104	
105	1. **One shape is the thread.** The arch is the loader's exit, the mid-page bowl with text on
106	   its rim, the pair of windows in the architecture act, and the closing frame. The visitor
107	   never names it, but the page feels like one building.
108	2. **Camera, not sections.** The hero is a descent; the amenities leave by zooming past the
109	   lens; the location turns the page sideways; the end pulls back into a window. Acts are
110	   *moves of one camera*, and each transition has a material cause (rule 2 of the floor).
111	3. **Alternation.** Full-bleed photo → cream text chapter → photo → pale-blue chapter. Never two
112	   dark photo acts in a row, never two text chapters in a row. Rest beats (the quote) every
113	   third act.
114	4. **One passage of a different axis.** A single horizontal stretch in a vertical page, placed
115	   after the first third, carrying the biggest type on the site.
116	5. **A living material that crosses the chapters.** Bougainvillea video loops bleed in from
117	   the frame edges in five different acts, each time larger or from another side.
118	6. **Text behaves the same way everywhere.** Every heading arrives the same way (chars standing
119	   up), every paragraph the same way (masked lines), every script word the same way — and then
120	   it stands still. Consistency of reveal is what lets the big moves read as big.
121	7. **The ending answers the opening.** Door in, window out.
122	8. **Tempo is set, not left to the wheel.** Lenis 1.2 s duration, chapters that snap, a hero of
123	   five screens, scrub values of 0.25–0.5 — slow enough that nothing is missed (F-020).

# The Era journey — era-residence.com broken down and rebuilt as a grammar

Catalogue entry: `design-catalogue/entries/era-residence/` (rank #1 in `ranking.txt`,
`motion_floor: 2`; `motion/sheet.webp` is the 20-step contact sheet, `motion/probe.json` the
stack). Read 2026-10-03 by the lead from the sheet, and from a static inventory of the site's
own motion file (Slater `60900.js`, 59 KB, agency THEFIRSTTHELAST).

Anton, 2026-10-03: *"själva resan på sidan, inte den exakta layouten eller utseendet, men det är
en sån typ av visuell resa jag vill skapa åt användarna på de sidor vi producerar, med olika
stil- och formspråk i övrigt, ingen sida får vara den andra lik."*

So this file describes the **trip** — what the visitor is carried through and how one act hands
over to the next — as something to rebuild with a different shape, material, palette and type
every time. It is not a layout to copy. The variation slots in § 5 are the point.

## 1. The stack (measured, not guessed)

Webflow page, no Webflow Interactions. **GSAP 3.15.0 with only ScrollTrigger, SplitText and
CustomEase registered** — no ScrollSmoother, no Flip, no SVG plugins, no WebGL, no three.js, no
shaders. **Lenis 1.3.21** (`duration 1.2`, `smoothWheel`, `touchMultiplier 2`, expo-style easing,
`lenis.on("scroll", ScrollTrigger.update)`, `gsap.ticker` drives `raf`, `lagSmoothing(0)`).
Barba 2.10.3 for page transitions. Lottie once (the agency credit). Eight bougainvillea video
loops (webm/mov, avif posters) played by ScrollTrigger on enter, paused on leave.

Everything rich on the page is **CSS mask / clip-path driven by GSAP, SplitText masks, `position:
sticky` + scrub, and timing**. The lesson for the chain: the showcase level is reached with two
plugins and discipline, not with a plugin inventory.

Motion tokens (mirrored as CSS variables):
```
durS 0.4   durM 0.8   durL 1.2   stagger 0.1   delayReveal 0.3
InOut  .75,0,.25,1   Out .25,1,.5,1   In .5,0,.75,0   Ease .25,.1,.25,1
Write  .333,0,.667,1   diveIn .6,0,0,1   horScroll .25,0,.75,1   loader: custom SVG path ease
html { font-size: 1vw }   breakpoint 992
```
Type: ambroise-francois-std (condensed display serif), sloop-script-three (script accent),
Maison Neue Extended (body). Ground: burgundy `#340C25`, sky/pool blues, cream, pale blue.

## 2. The journey, act by act

| # | Act (what the visitor sees) | Mechanism (what the code does) | House equivalent |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | **Burgundy overture.** Logo mark, the words of the place (Costa · del Sol) ghosted huge in script behind, the name in condensed serif with the town in script, a thin vertical rule, a one-line promise. A progress bar runs ~4 s on the first visit. | Preloader `position: fixed`, SplitText reveals, 1.2 s hold, bar with the custom `loaderEase`; `sessionStorage.hasVisited` → repeat visits skip to the dive. | Intro pattern "copy first" + rule 1 of `showcase-floor.md`: the overture's last frame is the hero's first. |
| 0→1 | **The arch dive.** An arch-shaped opening rises from the bottom of the burgundy screen, frames the sky, widens, and the camera flies *through* it onto the estate. | Three CSS rectangles + an arch SVG as `mask-image`; GSAP tweens `--arch-w` 24→36 vw and `--arch-y` 104→15 vh (1.5 s InOut), then 125 vw / −100 vh (2.4 s diveIn) while the hero photo scales 0.75→1 (1.15→1 on mobile). Barba starts 25 % into the dive. | The handoff is the brand's own architecture. On our pages: the signature shape (a window, a page corner, a lens, a letter counter) is the door. |
| 1 | **Hero: descent to the pool.** The title holds over the sky; the estate rises behind it; the text column and the tall background drift at different rates; then the photo zooms until we are over the water. | `.hero-w` sticky 100 vh inside a scroll area `calc(100vh*4 + 50rem + 100vh)`; scrubbed: two translate rates, then `scale 1→2` from `transform-origin 50% 75%` ("In" ease). | A pinned act of ~5 screens with **one** continuous camera move; heading still for ≥ 40 vh before the zoom (F-025). |
| 2 | **"A place to live, to return year after year."** A pale half-moon rises from the bottom with a sentence set along its curve; it grows until it is the next ground. | Section pulled up by `−(50rem + 100vh)` so it overlaps the zoom; SVG circle text with `wordSpacing` 0→10 rem scrubbed. | Transition cause "panel grows from the axis" + "text on the curve of the shape that frames the image" — the arch again, now as a bowl. |
| 3 | **Benefits as slides.** Real-life location · community, not complex · built to stay · boutique: a small photo card grows to full bleed, the next slides in. | `[data-snap]` section; Lenis custom snap (40 ms after stop, >50 % visible → `lenis.scrollTo`); the `slide` reveal = `clipPath polygon(100% 0,100% 0,101% 100%,125% 100%)` → full rectangle while the inner image goes from `scale 1.5, xPercent 25` to rest, 1.2 s InOut (a diagonal wipe with a counter-zoom). | "card-to-full-bleed grow". Our build: Flip or a clip-path scrub; snap through Lenis, never ScrollTrigger snap on the page. |
| 4 | **Quote.** A pull quote over a pool photo that parallaxes away. | `img-out` parallax (yPercent 0→20). | A rest beat. One per three acts. |
| 5 | **Location: the horizontal passage.** The page turns sideways: the concept, then "Spain / New / Golden / Mile" in huge serif whose lines drift at different offsets, "Between Marbella and Estepona", a hand-drawn route with stops that draws itself, flowers drifting past. | Section height = track width; sticky screen; `x: −(scrollWidth − width)` with `horScroll` ease, `scrub 0.25`, from "2.5% top" to "97.5% bottom"; title lines `wrap([-5,25,-15])→wrap([5,-25,25])`; path revealed by clip-path over 2.4 s; info block fades 0→1 and scales 0.75→1. Desktop only. | "horizontal pin pan" (Khanh). Reveals inside use `containerAnimation`. DrawSVG for the route. Mobile gets the same acts stacked. |
| 6 | **Master plan.** An aerial render settles; a cloud marquee crosses; three pulsing pins open floating tips. | Image `scale 1.15→1` scrubbed; `@keyframes` marquee 32 s with every even cloud flipped; pins with an infinite pulse ring; tips follow the cursor (2.4 s, power3). | The "object with hotspots" device; CSS does the marquee. |
| 7 | **Apartment types.** Three typologies in an auto slider with a progress bar. | 6 s per slide, paused by IntersectionObserver < 0.2; change = hide text (SplitText −110 %), wipe in the image (`slide`), reveal text. | A ledger-with-image act; the slide wipe is the recurring transition. |
| 8 | **Residences range from 104 to 244 m².** Rules and paragraphs reveal. | `line` reveal `clipPath inset(0 0 100% 0)→inset(0)`, `p` reveal masked lines `yPercent 110→0`. | Shared reveal, house-physics. |
| 9 | **Amenities.** Vertical tabs with a sliding highlight; on exit the whole content zooms past the camera while fading. | Sticky screen in a 2.5-screen area; scrubbed exit `scale 1→2`, wrapper `opacity 1→0`. | "exit through the lens" — the act leaves by the same camera that brought us in. |
| 10 | **Interior.** Accordion of upgrades, a gallery that opens a lightbox (zoom + pan). | Reuses the reveals; lightbox `scale 0.5→1`, slides ±125 %, smoothed mouse pan on desktop, pinch on mobile. | Read-mode pocket inside a persuade page. |
| 11 | **Architecture: the second arch.** "The space to live in" rises as a second half-moon; two window openings grow in a photo and open fully; the side flowers push outward; the frame scales from 0.75 to 1. | Sticky `.arch-w`, scrubbed "top bottom"→"200% top": two polygon clip-path masks; intro `scale 1→1.84`; flowers `scale` up and `xPercent ±50`; text reveals at "30% top"; image parallax 25 % from "55% top". Desktop only. | Rule 3: the signature object (arch + flowers) **recurs and changes** — overture door, mid-page bowl, now a pair of windows. |
| 12–13 | **Facts, CTA.** Developer, architects, licence, "a short conversation is enough". | Reveals. | Ledger + one action. |
| 14 | **Footer: the window closes.** The last photo shrinks from full bleed into a framed window — the arch's rectangle cousin — while the footer rises and the scroll cue fades. | Scrubbed from "top 30%": `clipPath inset(0)→inset(8% 22% 8% 22%)` (`4% 32%` mobile); footer content `opacity 0→1`, `scale 0.75→1`. | The ending answers the opening: we came in through an opening, we leave looking out through one. |

Always present: a fixed header whose logo spins on the ticker at 30 °/s ± 10·|Lenis velocity| (so
the mark breathes with the scroll), a desktop scrollbar with a 00–99 label, a scroll cue, and a
header that swaps light/dark/colour theme per section (`[data-bg]` triggers at the header's
centre line). Hover grammar: magnetic buttons (strength 25, power4 1.6 s, elastic release), nav
words rolling as two masked copies, link characters flipping ±90° with an underline that exits
right and re-enters left, circle buttons whose arc stroke grows 4 %→50 %, siblings dimming to 0.2
via `:has()`.

Reveal system (`[data-scroll-reveal]`, once at "top bottom"; inside the track via
`containerAnimation` at "left bottom"): `a` script accent (chars from opacity 0, rotateX 90,
x 10 rem, origin bottom; 1.2 s Out, stagger 0.1) · `h` headings (chars yPercent 50, rotateY 90;
stagger 0.05) · `p` paragraphs (masked lines yPercent 110→0; hide −110 in 0.4 s In) · `ctn`
blocks (y 3.333 rem, opacity 0) · `line` rules (clip inset) · `slide` images (diagonal wipe +
counter-zoom). Parallax: `img` ±15 % scrub 0.5, `img-in` −20→0, `img-out` 0→20, `ctn-up/down`
±10 from "top 125%" to "bottom −25%"; any of them switched off per breakpoint with
`data-mob="off"` / `data-desk="off"`.


### 2b. Seen at 60 frames (`MOTION_FRAMES=60`, 2026-10-03)

The 20-frame sheet hid how the acts hand over. At 60 frames each transition shows its material:

- **The bowl hands its colour on.** The half-moon of act 2 carries "Three reasons to choose Era"
  along its curve; it rises in pale sky blue and, fully grown, *is* the benefits section's ground.
  The transition and the next act are the same colour field. Nothing fades; the shape becomes the
  ground.
- **Flowers bridge the ground change.** Where pale blue turns to cream (benefits → concept), a
  bougainvillea cut-out enters from the lower edge first and the cream follows it, so the change
  has a cause on screen before it happens.
- **Clouds carry the route into the master plan.** The hand-drawn route of the horizontal passage
  runs into a bank of clouds; the clouds part onto the aerial render. Act 5 → 6 is a camera
  descending through weather, not a cut.
- **The reverse grow.** After the master plan the full-bleed aerial shrinks back into a framed
  card on pale blue (the typology slider). The same card ↔ full-bleed move is used in both
  directions, which is what makes it read as one system.
- **The overture's burgundy returns as blocks.** In "The space to live in" the burgundy of the
  first screen comes back as rectangular colour panels holding bougainvillea photos, and the
  closing "ARCHITECTURE" sets condensed type across the photograph (rule 5: type and media in one
  frame).

House reading: rule 2 of `showcase-floor.md` is met here by *one* material per transition (a
shape, a plant, weather, a card), each taken from the subject itself. That is the bar for the
Alunix next round (AUDIT-ALUNIX-R9.md § 4).

## 3. What makes it a journey (the part to keep)

1. **One shape is the thread.** The arch is the loader's exit, the mid-page bowl with text on
   its rim, the pair of windows in the architecture act, and the closing frame. The visitor
   never names it, but the page feels like one building.
2. **Camera, not sections.** The hero is a descent; the amenities leave by zooming past the
   lens; the location turns the page sideways; the end pulls back into a window. Acts are
   *moves of one camera*, and each transition has a material cause (rule 2 of the floor).
3. **Alternation.** Full-bleed photo → cream text chapter → photo → pale-blue chapter. Never two
   dark photo acts in a row, never two text chapters in a row. Rest beats (the quote) every
   third act.
4. **One passage of a different axis.** A single horizontal stretch in a vertical page, placed
   after the first third, carrying the biggest type on the site.
5. **A living material that crosses the chapters.** Bougainvillea video loops bleed in from
   the frame edges in five different acts, each time larger or from another side.
6. **Text behaves the same way everywhere.** Every heading arrives the same way (chars standing
   up), every paragraph the same way (masked lines), every script word the same way — and then
   it stands still. Consistency of reveal is what lets the big moves read as big.
7. **The ending answers the opening.** Door in, window out.
8. **Tempo is set, not left to the wheel.** Lenis 1.2 s duration, chapters that snap, a hero of
   five screens, scrub values of 0.25–0.5 — slow enough that nothing is missed (F-020).

## 4. Rebuild recipe (house toolchain)

Static HTML with the importmap from `toolchain.md`; `./gsap.js` exports `gsap, ScrollTrigger,
SplitText, CustomEase, Flip, DrawSVGPlugin`; `./smooth-scroll.js` exports the Lenis instance
with the house tempo (`lerp .075`, `wheelMultiplier .6`) — do not copy Era's Lenis numbers.

```js
import { gsap, ScrollTrigger, SplitText, CustomEase, DrawSVGPlugin } from "./gsap.js";
import lenis from "./smooth-scroll.js";

// tokens — rename per project, never reuse the values as a set
CustomEase.create("inOut", "0.75,0,0.25,1"); CustomEase.create("out", "0.25,1,0.5,1");
CustomEase.create("in", "0.5,0,0.75,0");     CustomEase.create("dive", "0.6,0,0,1");
const D = { s: 0.4, m: 0.8, l: 1.2, stagger: 0.1 };

// 0→1  the door: a masked opening that rises, widens, and we pass through
const door = gsap.timeline({ paused: true });
door.to(":root", { "--door-w": "36vw", "--door-y": "15vh", duration: 1.5, ease: "inOut" })
    .to(":root", { "--door-w": "125vw", "--door-y": "-100vh", duration: 2.4, ease: "dive" })
    .fromTo(".hero-plate", { scale: 0.75 }, { scale: 1, duration: 3.9, ease: "dive" }, 0);
// overture copy reveals first (SplitText masks), a hold, then door.play()

// 1  hero descent: ~5 screens, one camera move, heading still ≥ 40 vh
gsap.timeline({ scrollTrigger: { trigger: ".hero-area", start: "top top", end: "bottom bottom", scrub: 0.5 } })
  .to(".hero-copy", { yPercent: -40, ease: "none" }, 0)
  .to(".hero-plate", { yPercent: -15, ease: "none" }, 0)
  .to({}, { duration: 0.35 })                                            // the still beat
  .to(".hero-plate", { scale: 2, transformOrigin: "50% 75%", ease: "in" });
// .hero-area is 500vh tall; .hero-w is position: sticky; top: 0; height: 100vh

// 2  the bowl: a shape rises and grows into the next ground, its rim carrying a sentence
gsap.timeline({ scrollTrigger: { trigger: ".bowl", start: "top bottom", end: "top top", scrub: 0.4 } })
  .fromTo(".bowl-shape", { yPercent: 60, scale: 0.8 }, { yPercent: 0, scale: 1.6, ease: "none" })
  .to(".bowl-rim-text", { attr: { "word-spacing": "10rem" } }, 0);     // <textPath> on the arc

// 3  slide wipe (the recurring image transition)
const wipeIn = (img) => gsap.timeline()
  .fromTo(img.parentElement, { clipPath: "polygon(100% 0,100% 0,101% 100%,125% 100%)" },
          { clipPath: "polygon(0 0,100% 0,100% 100%,0 100%)", duration: D.l, ease: "inOut" })
  .fromTo(img, { scale: 1.5, xPercent: 25 }, { scale: 1, xPercent: 0, duration: D.l, ease: "inOut" }, 0);

// 5  the sideways passage
const track = document.querySelector(".track");
const pan = gsap.to(track, { x: () => -(track.scrollWidth - innerWidth), ease: "none",
  scrollTrigger: { trigger: ".passage", pin: true, start: "top top", scrub: 0.25,
                   end: () => "+=" + (track.scrollWidth - innerWidth), invalidateOnRefresh: true } });
gsap.fromTo("#route", { drawSVG: "0%" }, { drawSVG: "100%", ease: "none",
  scrollTrigger: { containerAnimation: pan, trigger: "#route", start: "left 70%", end: "right 40%", scrub: 0.4 } });

// 14  the window closes
gsap.timeline({ scrollTrigger: { trigger: ".outro", start: "top 30%", end: "bottom bottom", scrub: 0.5 } })
  .to(".outro-plate", { clipPath: "inset(8% 22% 8% 22%)", ease: "none" })
  .fromTo(".footer", { autoAlpha: 0, scale: 0.75 }, { autoAlpha: 1, scale: 1, ease: "none" }, 0);

// text, the same way everywhere
document.fonts.ready.then(() => {
  SplitText.create("[data-reveal=p]", { type: "lines", mask: "lines", autoSplit: true,
    onSplit: s => gsap.from(s.lines, { yPercent: 110, duration: D.l, ease: "out", stagger: D.stagger,
      scrollTrigger: { trigger: s.elements[0], start: "top 85%", once: true } }) });
  SplitText.create("[data-reveal=h]", { type: "chars,words", autoSplit: true,
    onSplit: s => gsap.from(s.chars, { yPercent: 50, rotateY: 90, autoAlpha: 0, duration: D.m, ease: "out", stagger: 0.05,
      scrollTrigger: { trigger: s.elements[0], start: "top 85%", once: true } }) });
});

// chapter snap through Lenis (never ScrollTrigger snap at page level)
let t; lenis.on("scroll", () => { clearTimeout(t); t = setTimeout(() => {
  const hit = [...document.querySelectorAll("[data-snap]")].find(s => { const r = s.getBoundingClientRect();
    return Math.min(r.bottom, innerHeight) - Math.max(r.top, 0) > innerHeight * 0.5 && r.top !== 0; });
  hit && lenis.scrollTo(hit, { duration: 1.2 }); }, 60); });
```

Verification stays the house's: `section_probe.py` on the whole page against the baseline
(F-021), `motion_probe.py` for staircase/frame time (F-013), the contact sheet read by the lead,
and the two floor-2 references open beside it (`showcase-floor.md` § 1).

## 5. Variation slots — how the next page is *not* Era

Fill every slot differently from Era and from the last house page; the fingerprint gate
(`feel-and-fingerprint.md`) checks it, but decide it here first.

| Slot | Era | Other answers seen in the catalogue |
|---|---|---|
| The thread shape | an arch (architecture) | a lens (elegantseagulls), a letter counter (khanhnguyen's parting word), a window in a photo (Hōrai), a vinyl (lesburgersdecolette), a cube unfolding (d2c-lifescience), a pen standing in the sentence (nota), a bolt that wipes (agencefoudre) |
| The door (overture → hero) | fly through the shape | counter → mark (ddark, nickho), copy first then light (seewhateyesee), curtain/push (filmbot), letters out of blur (millemann), object in the loader (ikea), pixel-block dissolve (davidecattaneo, meesverberne) |
| The camera | descent, then zoom past | dolly into a drawing (illoca), corridor of photos (thisisonward), orbit a product (neiru), a walk through rooms (maximeguillon), a room of text (stabondar) |
| The living material | flower video loops at the edges | smoke, grain, paper fibre, a drifting cloud marquee, cut-out people (vazzi), stickers, a ribbon (digidop) |
| The passage of a different axis | one horizontal location chapter | a vertical column wall (markclennon), a checkerboard swap (thomasmonavon), a tilted plane (wodniack), a 3D ring (annnimate) |
| The reveal grammar | chars standing up / masked lines | words lighting grey→ink (forge, filmbot), lines through blur (12 studio), scramble (modus), letters bobbing (flashform) |
| The rest beat | a quote over a parallax pool | a single full-bleed still, a line drawing, silence on a flat ground |
| The ending | the photo becomes a framed window | the shape returns as the sign-off (heart mask → staircase, maelruffini), the wordmark melts back (thisisbond), Hello/Bye bookends (huge), the loader object sprints across the lab (runrobrun) |
| Tempo | Lenis 1.2 s, snap, scrub .25–.5 | house tempo fixed; vary act length and the position of the peak instead |

Rule of thumb: change the **shape, the material and the door** and the page is already its own;
keep the eight journey properties in § 3 and it will still feel like a trip.

## 6. Below the floor on Era itself (not to copy)

- `prefers-reduced-motion` is not read anywhere — consistent with the house (F-011), noted
  only because the a11y audit will ask.
- No `<img>` has `width`/`height`; srcset tops at 1920 w; `html { font-size: 1vw }` makes
  every rem scale with the viewport (type gets very small on narrow desktops).
- A Swiper init that never runs (dead code), and the location and architecture acts are
  desktop-only — mobile gets a flatter page. The house version keeps the acts on mobile as
  stacked scenes.
- First-visit-only overture via `sessionStorage`: fine, but the repeat-visit door must still
  satisfy rule 1 (something persists across the handoff) — on Era it does, the dive stays.

# Scroll · Step 2b — Grammar, feeling curve, signature move, fingerprint

Where vendored scroll-craft (`../upstream/scroll-craft/`) plugs into `design`.
Runs between Step 2 (the gate) and Step 4 (build), only on a Persuade/
Experience surface whose brief actually asked for scroll choreography.

## The scope rule (verbatim)

> Persuade/Experience surfaces (landing, marketing, portfolio, campaign) MUST
> ship ≥4 device families, never the same device twice in a row, one
> engineered peak with the largest span, one signature move, and pass the
> fingerprint gate; Operate/Read surfaces (dashboards, admin, settings, docs)
> get NO scroll choreography (frequency rule: 100+/day = no animation) —
> state motion 150–250 ms only; ~~reduced motion removes travel, not content~~ (**utgår, F-011** — see below).

The Operate/Read half is not new: it's `../motion.md`'s existing scroll-
linked-motion ban (reveal-once only, no casual parallax, no scrub), restated in
scroll-craft's vocabulary. Nothing here overrides `../../SKILL.md` § Product
surfaces for an authenticated page.

The rule's closing clause — ~~"reduced motion removes travel"~~ — **utgår per F-011 (2026-09-07)**.
No build reads a motion preference at all, so
there is **no such path (F-011)** for the clause to describe. What it was
protecting survives on its own terms and is not a preference: **no device may
make content unreachable**. A `pan` rail's transform is the navigation, so
every item in it stays gettable, and that is confirmed on the contact sheet.
See [`devices.md`](devices.md) § Rail settle.

## Contract

**Reads** — the `design` Step 1 interview (scroll-craft's eight questions
fold in, not asked twice); [`grammars.md`](grammars.md) (pick one grammar
against the register); [`devices.md`](devices.md) (nine devices, cue
contract); [`feel-and-fingerprint.md`](feel-and-fingerprint.md) (curve, peak,
move, gate); the registry `VAULT/wiki/projects/_index/design-fingerprints.md`;
`../house-physics.md` Motion + `../motion.md` — output must clear both bars.

**Does** — names the grammar and states why the other seven lost; writes the
feeling curve (emotion → cause per act) and names the peak; invents one
signature move, bespoke and coded in the page, never a kit parameter tweak;
scores the journey into a device table (≥4 families, never twice running, ≤2
`scrub`); runs the fingerprint gate against every existing registry row (≥4
of 6 dimensions clear, per row).

**Writes** — `BRIEF.md` additions (feeling curve, peak sentence,
tell-someone sentence, signature move); the score table (beat → device →
why); one new registry row, appended after ship.

**Human checks** — the fingerprint result is shown, not asserted (≥4-of-6
printed against every row, not "it passed"); the feel check
([`feel-and-fingerprint.md`](feel-and-fingerprint.md) § Peak: scroll cold,
one word per act, diff against the intended curve before opening `BRIEF.md`);
the verification JSON pasted, not summarized (`scroll_verify.py`, generic, or
scroll-craft's own `shoot.mjs` on the real engine); a human reads the contact
sheet — no automated pass above substitutes for that.

### What the harness cannot tell you

Upstream `verify.md` § What the harness cannot tell you names three, and they
are *"the ones that matter most"*. Read the sheet for them; a green run says
nothing about any of the three.

- **Whether the motion is smooth.** *"Contiguous frames prove the clip
  advances; they do not prove it advances evenly."* Watch the contact sheet
  for a move that lurches, reverses, or stalls in the middle. This is the
  sentence that explains F-012: every mechanical check passed while the page
  looked cheap. The chain's answer is not to trust the sheet either — it is
  `motion_probe.py` plus a cold human scroll; see
  [`../motion-smoothness.md`](../motion-smoothness.md) and [`pace.md`](pace.md).
- **Whether the composition is any good.** Copy landing on the busiest part of
  the frame, a subject cropped at an unfortunate point, an act whose end frame
  is a dark empty corner.
- **Whether the page means anything.** *"Six acts that each work and together
  say nothing is the most expensive failure available here."*

Two more the harness structurally cannot reach: **pan overflow** (a rail
narrower than the viewport travels zero and reports `no dead scroll detected`
on every pass — measure `rail.scrollWidth - innerWidth` by hand), and **the
phone**, which is a different machine. Headless Chrome cannot reproduce an
iPhone's video decoder, autoplay policy, Low Power Mode or touch scrolling: on
one upstream build every probe reported the hero clip scrubbing perfectly for
**four consecutive rounds while the real phone showed a frozen frame**.

### The spacer is sized once, at mount

Worth knowing before blaming the motion for anything, and a live candidate
whenever a build is judged inside an embedded preview panel rather than a real
tab. In worldflight mode the engine writes the spacer height as
`(total + 1) * innerHeight` **once**, inside mount. If `innerHeight` reports 0
at that moment the spacer is set to **0 px**, the page has no scroll track,
and the flight never advances.

> *"It fails silently and it looks like success."* The engine mounted, every
> leg registered, the clips fetched and decoded, and there is nothing in the
> console. The page is simply a still image that cannot be scrolled. Embedded
> preview panes and some early loads do exactly this.

**Do not fix it in the engine** (`NOTE.md`: the engine is never edited). One
resize makes it re-measure correctly, so the *page* sends one once the window
and the fonts have settled:

```js
function relayout() { dispatchEvent(new Event('resize')); }
addEventListener('load', relayout);
if (document.fonts && document.fonts.ready) document.fonts.ready.then(relayout);
```

The `fonts.ready` half earns its place independently: a webfont swapping in
changes the measured height of every copy block, so anything sized against
those blocks is wrong until it re-measures.

Check it in one line, **before** blaming anything else:

```js
document.documentElement.scrollHeight   // ≈ (sum of weights + 1) * innerHeight
```

- [`devices.md`](devices.md) — the nine devices + the cue contract's gotchas.

  the catalogue): acts, mechanisms, the eight properties that make it a trip, a rebuild recipe

- [`toolchain.md`](toolchain.md) — how GSAP + Lenis are linked, imported and verified here.
- [`pace.md`](pace.md) — the third "not smooth" fault: uneven rate, the
  0.21–0.22 vh/s floor, worldflight's `data-sc-lerp` 0.12 / `data-sc-seam` 0.16.
- Full upstream source for anything condensed here:
  `../upstream/scroll-craft/plugins/nateherk-design/skills/scroll-craft/`.
- Engine + starting template (copy per project, never edit it):
  `../../scripts/scroll/` — `scrollcraft.js`, `.css`, `template.html`, `NOTE.md`.
- Generic verification harness: `../../scripts/scroll_verify.py`.

**Engine is opt-in per grammar (AB06).** Use the vendored engine only when the chosen grammar needs scrub, pin or pan acts, and never in a blind one-shot: build, read the console for `[scrollcraft]` warnings, run `scroll_verify.py`, fix, repeat. Otherwise the chain's own signature set-piece + shared reveal (house-physics) is the default.

## Cited, not condensed

Read these upstream files directly when the build reaches them. Nothing below
is summarised anywhere in the chain, and each is the only place its content
exists.

| Upstream file | Read it for |
|---|---|
| `references/worldflight.md` | The markup, the scroll track and spacer maths, the **one-sided seam**, the copy contract (**windows ≤ 4 vh**), the route rail and `sc:waypoint`, and the **seam law for assets** (a leg's last frame and the next leg's first frame must match, GOP boundaries included). §§ 7b and 7c are condensed here and in [`pace.md`](pace.md); the rest is not |
| `scripts/worldflight-assert.mjs` | **The only automatic lerp-convergence and non-overshoot check in the whole corpus.** Nothing in `scroll_verify.py` or `motion_probe.py` does what it does; if a flight is being built, run it |

| `references/verify.md` § The phone is a different machine | The iOS clip lifecycle: metadata priming, `touchend` (not `touchstart`) as the activation event, the 2 s prime-flag release, re-issuing a seek stuck past 700 ms, the 2.5 s poster-reveal timeout. | `references/worlds.md` | The eight world preambles: what a scene is made of before any device touches it |
| `EXAMPLES.md` | Twelve filled fingerprint rows with the numbers inline. The `orrery` row is the worked example of the pace bar: ten legs, every 5 s leg at 1.08 vh and the 10 s peak at 2.25, **0.212–0.225 vh/s everywhere**, `data-sc-seam` 0.16, `data-sc-lerp` 0.12, measured spread 6% down from 36%. 1	# The eight page grammars
2	
3	Condensed from `upstream/scroll-craft/.../references/uniqueness.md` §2 — read
4	that file for the full text, the worked "four sites, one template" finding,
5	and the reasoning behind each forbid. A grammar is the page's organising
6	logic, not its palette: two pages in the same grammar feel related no matter
7	how far apart their worlds are. Pick exactly one; never blend two.
8	
9	| Grammar | Fits | Scroll feels like | Forbids | Nav / hero / close | Leans on | Bans |
10	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
11	| **Filmic one-shot** | Single linear emotional arc — launches, consumer products | A film pushing through, no seams | Visible sequence, hard cuts, more than one entry point | Fixed minimal bar; full-bleed scrub hero, corner headline; pinned spotlight close, magnetic CTA | `scrub`, `pin`, `drift`, `kinetic` | Nothing structural — carries a burden of proof instead |
12	| **Chaptered editorial** | Long-form substance — method, manifesto, founder story | Turning pages, hard cuts between chapters | Continuous `drift`, full-bleed scrub hero, magnetic CTA, centred hero copy | No fixed bar; folio in margin; title-page hero (no media); colophon close, CTA as running text | `flow`+`in`, `reveal` at boundaries, `parallax` in a column, `count` in prose | `scrub` beyond one chapter, `spotlight`, `magnet` |
13	| **Live surface** | Software, tools, dashboards — the demo IS the argument | Operating something, panels populate | Any marketing chrome, full-bleed photography, kinetic headlines | App chrome (sidebar/tabs) as nav; hero is the product mid-state; close is a real input field | `pin`, `count` on real telemetry, pointer devices in-product | `scrub`, `kinetic`, `spotlight`, `drift` past two stops |
14	| **Continuous world** | A journey with real geography — supply chain, a place, a build | Moving through one space that never cuts | Section boundaries, any act device, second stage, interpolated `drift` | Nav is a map/waypoint list; hero is an establishing position; close is arrival at a place | worldflight legs, `data-sc-linger`, `sc:waypoint` | Every act device, `flow`, `pan`, hard cuts, `src` swaps |
15	| **Typographic poster** | A brand whose asset is a sentence — manifestos, agencies | Words at wildly different weights, rhythm from scale | Photographic ground, scrims, cards, decorative motion | Wordmark at composition scale; hero is one word/line at extreme scale; close inverts to smallest type, plain link | `kinetic`, `pin` with `--sc-p`-driven scale, `reveal` as a wipe | `scrub`, `pan` rails, `tilt`, `parallax` on text |
16	| **Gallery / catalog** | A range — products, portfolio, menu, materials | Walking a room, objects at their own pace | Argument-shaped pinned type, single hero claim, persuasion copy | Nav is an index that jumps; hero is object one, already labelled; close is last object or inquiry-as-label | `pan` as the spine, `reveal` per object, `tilt`, `count` | `kinetic` headlines, `spotlight`, `magnet`, >1 `scrub` |
17	| **Split stage** | Any two-sided argument — before/after, manual vs automated | Watching a balance tip toward a resolve | Full-bleed before the resolve, centred copy, symmetric close | No bar; divider IS the chrome; hero shows the split 50/50; close is the collapse to one column | `pin` with divider from `--sc-p`, `reveal` per side, real `count` | `pan`, `spotlight`, `magnet`, >1 `scrub`, `drift` |
18	| **Rhythmic cutlist** | Energy brands — streetwear, sport, events, music | A cut every second, 12–20 short sections | Any act >~1.4vh, `dwell`>0.1, `pin`, overlapping cues | Loud/marquee bar; hero cuts to next in under a viewport; close is abrupt full bleed | `flow`+`in` at short stagger, `reveal` on nearly every section, hard `drift` steps | `pin`, `spotlight`, `magnet`, `dwell`, `parallax` |
19	
20	Cutlist's peak problem — it bans the devices a peak normally wants — is
21	solved by moving the peak into the fixed chrome layer rather than breaking
22	the grammar; see uniqueness.md §2.8.
23	
24	## Two grammars carry a hard precondition
25	
26	Both are the kind of thing that is discovered a full build too late. Check
27	them at grammar selection, not at verification.
28	
29	### Live surface: the honesty rule (§2.3)
30	
31	The page behaves like the product — *"not a screenshot of it, and not a
32	div-built fake: the actual surface, running, with scroll driving its state."*
33	`taste.md`'s ban on fake dashboards and fake terminals is **not suspended
34	here**, and this grammar is where it is most tempting to suspend it.
35	
36	> The surface has to be **real markup running real logic on real or
37	> clearly-labelled sample data.**
38	
39	That labelled-sample escape is the whole way in for a **concept product**:
40	every panel is operable markup computing its state from data arrays in the
41	page, and **the page says on its face that the scenario is a demo**. Both
42	halves are required — operable, and labelled.
43	
44	What stays banned is *"the painting of a surface"*: an image, or dummy divs,
45	posing as something that runs. **If the panels cannot actually compute, the
46	grammar is unavailable. Pick another.** This is a build-feasibility question
47	disguised as a style choice, so answer it before the score table exists.
48	
49	Note the shape of the close this implies: *"a magnetic button is the wrong
50	ending for a page that spent its whole length being a tool"* — the close is an
51	**actual input** the visitor can put a cursor in.
52	
53	### Continuous world requires worldflight (§2.4)
54	
55	> **This grammar REQUIRES worldflight mode.** `data-sc-mode="worldflight"`,
56	> one fixed stage, one spacer, legs that crossfade.
57	
58	Building it out of pinned acts is **not a lesser version of this grammar, it
59	is a different and worse page**, and it has already been tried. The owner's
60	verdict on the act-based attempt:
61	
62	> *"awful… you're literally going from scrolling down to static page and then
63	> you start scrolling down again… weird clear page lines scrolling up… very
64	> cheap looking."*
65	
66	Every one of those is the same defect. **A pinned act is a block in the
67	document; a document made of blocks has seams; and a world with seams is not a
68	world.** Do not reach for `scrub` acts here, however long the spans are made.
69	
70	This is also the expensive one: *"a single unbroken flight is the most fragile
71	thing you can build"*, the seam law is not optional, and the build should be
72	budgeted with a reroll in it. Choose this grammar only when the brief is
73	literally about travel through a place. Its pace bar has its own file —
74	[`pace.md`](pace.md).
75	
76	## Register × grammar fit
77	
78	The six registers are `../../SKILL.md` § The craft floor's own list. Each row
79	below is 2–3 grammars that genuinely fit that register, plus one grammar that

# The eight page grammars

Condensed from `upstream/scroll-craft/.../references/uniqueness.md` §2 — read
that file for the full text, the worked "four sites, one template" finding,
and the reasoning behind each forbid. A grammar is the page's organising
logic, not its palette: two pages in the same grammar feel related no matter
how far apart their worlds are. Pick exactly one; never blend two.

| Grammar | Fits | Scroll feels like | Forbids | Nav / hero / close | Leans on | Bans |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Filmic one-shot** | Single linear emotional arc — launches, consumer products | A film pushing through, no seams | Visible sequence, hard cuts, more than one entry point | Fixed minimal bar; full-bleed scrub hero, corner headline; pinned spotlight close, magnetic CTA | `scrub`, `pin`, `drift`, `kinetic` | Nothing structural — carries a burden of proof instead |
| **Chaptered editorial** | Long-form substance — method, manifesto, founder story | Turning pages, hard cuts between chapters | Continuous `drift`, full-bleed scrub hero, magnetic CTA, centred hero copy | No fixed bar; folio in margin; title-page hero (no media); colophon close, CTA as running text | `flow`+`in`, `reveal` at boundaries, `parallax` in a column, `count` in prose | `scrub` beyond one chapter, `spotlight`, `magnet` |
| **Live surface** | Software, tools, dashboards — the demo IS the argument | Operating something, panels populate | Any marketing chrome, full-bleed photography, kinetic headlines | App chrome (sidebar/tabs) as nav; hero is the product mid-state; close is a real input field | `pin`, `count` on real telemetry, pointer devices in-product | `scrub`, `kinetic`, `spotlight`, `drift` past two stops |
| **Continuous world** | A journey with real geography — supply chain, a place, a build | Moving through one space that never cuts | Section boundaries, any act device, second stage, interpolated `drift` | Nav is a map/waypoint list; hero is an establishing position; close is arrival at a place | worldflight legs, `data-sc-linger`, `sc:waypoint` | Every act device, `flow`, `pan`, hard cuts, `src` swaps |
| **Typographic poster** | A brand whose asset is a sentence — manifestos, agencies | Words at wildly different weights, rhythm from scale | Photographic ground, scrims, cards, decorative motion | Wordmark at composition scale; hero is one word/line at extreme scale; close inverts to smallest type, plain link | `kinetic`, `pin` with `--sc-p`-driven scale, `reveal` as a wipe | `scrub`, `pan` rails, `tilt`, `parallax` on text |
| **Gallery / catalog** | A range — products, portfolio, menu, materials | Walking a room, objects at their own pace | Argument-shaped pinned type, single hero claim, persuasion copy | Nav is an index that jumps; hero is object one, already labelled; close is last object or inquiry-as-label | `pan` as the spine, `reveal` per object, `tilt`, `count` | `kinetic` headlines, `spotlight`, `magnet`, >1 `scrub` |
| **Split stage** | Any two-sided argument — before/after, manual vs automated | Watching a balance tip toward a resolve | Full-bleed before the resolve, centred copy, symmetric close | No bar; divider IS the chrome; hero shows the split 50/50; close is the collapse to one column | `pin` with divider from `--sc-p`, `reveal` per side, real `count` | `pan`, `spotlight`, `magnet`, >1 `scrub`, `drift` |
| **Rhythmic cutlist** | Energy brands — streetwear, sport, events, music | A cut every second, 12–20 short sections | Any act >~1.4vh, `dwell`>0.1, `pin`, overlapping cues | Loud/marquee bar; hero cuts to next in under a viewport; close is abrupt full bleed | `flow`+`in` at short stagger, `reveal` on nearly every section, hard `drift` steps | `pin`, `spotlight`, `magnet`, `dwell`, `parallax` |

Cutlist's peak problem — it bans the devices a peak normally wants — is
solved by moving the peak into the fixed chrome layer rather than breaking
the grammar; see uniqueness.md §2.8.

## Two grammars carry a hard precondition

Both are the kind of thing that is discovered a full build too late. Check
them at grammar selection, not at verification.

### Live surface: the honesty rule (§2.3)

The page behaves like the product — *"not a screenshot of it, and not a
div-built fake: the actual surface, running, with scroll driving its state."*
`taste.md`'s ban on fake dashboards and fake terminals is **not suspended
here**, and this grammar is where it is most tempting to suspend it.

> The surface has to be **real markup running real logic on real or
> clearly-labelled sample data.**

That labelled-sample escape is the whole way in for a **concept product**:
every panel is operable markup computing its state from data arrays in the
page, and **the page says on its face that the scenario is a demo**. Both
halves are required — operable, and labelled.

What stays banned is *"the painting of a surface"*: an image, or dummy divs,
posing as something that runs. **If the panels cannot actually compute, the
grammar is unavailable. Pick another.** This is a build-feasibility question
disguised as a style choice, so answer it before the score table exists.

Note the shape of the close this implies: *"a magnetic button is the wrong
ending for a page that spent its whole length being a tool"* — the close is an
**actual input** the visitor can put a cursor in.

### Continuous world requires worldflight (§2.4)

> **This grammar REQUIRES worldflight mode.** `data-sc-mode="worldflight"`,
> one fixed stage, one spacer, legs that crossfade.

Building it out of pinned acts is **not a lesser version of this grammar, it
is a different and worse page**, and it has already been tried. The owner's
verdict on the act-based attempt:

> *"awful… you're literally going from scrolling down to static page and then
> you start scrolling down again… weird clear page lines scrolling up… very
> cheap looking."*

Every one of those is the same defect. **A pinned act is a block in the
document; a document made of blocks has seams; and a world with seams is not a
world.** Do not reach for `scrub` acts here, however long the spans are made.

This is also the expensive one: *"a single unbroken flight is the most fragile
thing you can build"*, the seam law is not optional, and the build should be
budgeted with a reroll in it. Choose this grammar only when the brief is
literally about travel through a place. Its pace bar has its own file —
[`pace.md`](pace.md).

## Register × grammar fit

The six registers are `../../SKILL.md` § The craft floor's own list. Each row
below is 2–3 grammars that genuinely fit that register, plus one grammar that
reads as a mismatch and the one-line reason why.

| Register | Fits | Mismatch (and why) |
|---|---|---|
| **Editorial print** | Chaptered editorial (the register's native shape); Gallery/catalog (museum-label copy is already this register's voice); Typographic poster (a manifesto-led atelier) | Rhythmic cutlist — a loud marquee bar and hard-cut energy contradicts the register's restraint and apparatus |
| **Cinematic dark** | Filmic one-shot (linear narrative arc, hospitality/launch); Continuous world (atmosphere as geography — a restaurant, a hotel); Gallery/catalog (a menu as a walkable collection) | Typographic poster — the grammar bans photographic ground outright, and cinematic dark's whole effect is atmosphere built from photography |
| **Illustrated dark** | Typographic poster (strong verbal identity paired with drawn forms); Gallery/catalog (a set of speaker/object portraits as objects); Chaptered editorial (a programme read as chapters) | Live surface — the grammar bans marketing chrome and kinetic headlines, which is exactly the illustrated-identity apparatus this register is built from |
| **Modern clean** | Live surface (the subject is precision — an instrument, a technical firm); Split stage (a before/after comparison, cost vs saving); Typographic poster (minimal photography, the claim carries it) | Rhythmic cutlist — a loud, marqueed, cut-every-second page fights a register whose whole case is calm precision |
| **Warm photographic** | Filmic one-shot (a consumer/hospitality arc); Continuous world (a journey through a place — harbour, guesthouse); Gallery/catalog (rooms or dishes as a walkable range) | Typographic poster — same conflict as cinematic dark: the register's asset is the photograph, and the grammar has no photographic ground at all |
| **Historical art** | Gallery/catalog (museum labels are this grammar's literal copy schema); Chaptered editorial (an institution that plausibly publishes an edition or catalogue); Continuous world (a journey through a collection or a period) | Rhythmic cutlist — a loud, marqueed, energy-brand grammar reads as flippant against institutional gravitas |

Cite `upstream/scroll-craft/plugins/nateherk-design/skills/scroll-craft/references/uniqueness.md`
for the full grammar text, the fingerprint gate, and the signature-move rules
(the latter two are condensed separately in
[`feel-and-fingerprint.md`](feel-and-fingerprint.md)).

1	# Feeling curve, peak, signature move, fingerprint gate
2	
3	Condensed from `upstream/scroll-craft/.../references/feel.md` and
4	`uniqueness.md` §§3–4. Design the feeling before the acts: a device chosen
5	before the emotion is a device looking for a reason.
6	
7	## The feeling curve
8	
9	One line per act in `BRIEF.md`, written **before a single act exists**: the
10	emotion, then what on screen causes it. The emotion is the constraint; the
11	device name only ever appears in the cause column, second.
12	
13	```
14	1  Recognition   their own kitchen counter at 7am, shot at eye height
15	2  Fatigue       the two containers, the mess, held still while copy names it
16	3  Delight       a wipe, and the whole frame is one cold can, condensation running
17	4  Trust         macro texture at a scale the eye cannot get in a shop
18	5  Appetite      the flavours travelling sideways, each one landing whole
19	6  Resolve       everything stops, one can, one line, one place to buy it
20	```
21	
22	Two adjacent acts with the same feeling means one is filler — cut it or
23	change what it does. The curve outranks the Step 1 journey beats: beats say
24	what the visitor learns, the curve says what they feel while learning it, and
25	where they disagree the curve wins.
26	
27	## The peak
28	
29	People remember one peak and the ending; the middle compresses into a general
30	impression. So every build engineers **one** deliberate peak, named in
31	`BRIEF.md` as the sentence a visitor would say to a friend ("the screen went
32	black and then the whole ocean lit up under me" — a moment, not "the hero is
33	impressive"). The peak gets, at the expense of every other act:
34	
35	| It gets | Because |
36	|---|---|
37	| The asset budget | Best generated frames or the only real footage go here |
38	| The silence before it | A quiet act or empty viewport, so the change has something to be a change from |
39	| The most scroll room | Largest `data-sc-span` on the page, `dwell` tuned to settle exactly there |
40	
41	A page with three peaks has none — demote the losers (shorter span, plainer
42	device). The close must resolve, not trail off: the divider collapses, the
43	world lands somewhere, the type quiets — never a fade to an empty stage.
44	
45	## The tell-someone test
46	
47	Complete, before building: *"it's the site where ___."* "It has a scrub
48	video" is a device name — no hook. "You drag the letters of the logo apart
49	and they snap back perfectly" is an experience — that's a hook. The blank has
50	to be something that happened **to the visitor**. This sentence usually
51	contains the signature move; if the tell-someone sentence and the signature
52	move point at different moments, one of them is decoration.
53	
54	## The signature move
55	
56	One bespoke interaction that exists on this build alone — coded in the page
57	off `--sc-p` or a page-authored `data-sc-*`, never a parameter on a kit
58	device, never in any prior build. The engine stays untouched.
59	
60	**What counts** (upstream examples, not a menu to pick from): scroll-as-
61	playhead over a persistent trace rail; a wordmark the pointer pulls apart and
62	snaps back exactly; a line drawing whose `stroke-dashoffset` is driven from
63	`--sc-p`; a running receipt that accumulates real figures; one control that
64	regrades the whole page at once (time-of-day, temperature, load).
65	
66	**What does not count**: a recoloured/resized spotlight; `data-sc-tilt` turned
67	up; a different easing on kinetic lines; more cards in a rail; a third
68	`scrub` act; anything the engine already does under a project class name.
69	Test: describe the move to someone who has seen the other builds — if they
70	can't tell it apart from something the kit already does, it isn't one.
71	
72	## Being in it, not watching it
73	
74	Upstream `feel.md` § 4. *"A film plays whether you are there or not. The
75	difference between a viewer and a participant is whether the page acknowledges
76	that somebody specific is here: how fast they are moving, where their pointer
77	is, whether they stopped."*
78	
79	Five techniques, in the kit's own vocabulary:
80	
81	- **Pointer parallax that moves the world, not a card.** `data-sc-spotlight`
82	  publishes `--sc-mx` / `--sc-my`. Drive a *background layer's* transform off
83	  them instead of a highlight, and the environment shifts as the visitor
84	  moves, slightly, the way a real space does when you lean.
85	- **Dwell-triggered detail.** Hold still on an act and something further
86	  arrives — a caption, a second line, a small annotation. Reward for stopping.
87	  Mechanically: **read `--sc-p` staying constant across a few frames**, in the
88	  page's own JS, and reveal something that was **never needed for
89	  comprehension**.
90	- **Scroll velocity shaping intensity.** Fast scrolling raises grain, blur,
91	  chromatic offset, ground saturation; slow scrolling settles it. *"The page
92	  feels like it is being driven rather than played back, and it costs one
93	  derived custom property."*
94	- **The page addressing "you" at one moment that lands.** Not throughout,
95	  which is just copywriting. **One line**, at the emotional turn, in second
96	  person, when the visitor is already implicated. *"It works because it is the
97	  only time."*
98	- **A trace of where they have been.** Anything that accumulates as they
99	  travel, so arriving at the end means having a record rather than reaching a
100	  footer.
101	
102	**Embodiment is seasoning. One or two per page.** *"A page that reacts to
103	everything feels haunted, not alive: the visitor stops reading and starts
104	poking, which is the opposite of what any of this is for."* Pick the one that
105	serves the peak and leave the rest.
106	
107	These are gated to `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` — a pointer-capability
108	query, which stands.
109	Upstream also turns them off under reduced motion — **that half utgår, F-011**.
110	The rule that does survive is upstream's own:
111	*"a technique that only exists on desktop cannot be the thing that carries the
112	page's meaning."*
113	
114	## Pacing as emotion
115	
116	Upstream `feel.md` § 5. *"Scroll distance is emotional time. It is the only
117	clock this medium has, and it is fully under your control, which makes it the
118	cheapest emotional instrument in the kit and the one most often left at
119	default."*
120	
121	| Pacing | Reads as | Built with |
122	|---|---|---|
123	| Short acts, hard cuts | Adrenaline, pulse, impatience | Acts under 1.4 vh, no `pin`, `dwell` at 0 |
124	| A long pin | Held breath, pressure, attention | `data-sc-span` 3+, overlapping cues, one idea |
125	| An empty viewport before a reveal | Silence before the drop | A ground-only act, no cue until the next one |
126	| A slow settle mid-act | The shot landing | `data-sc-dwell` 0.35–0.6, cue peak on the settle |
127	| A fast cue with a long plateau | Confidence, arrival | `data-sc-cue="0.1 0.9 0.08 0.4"` |
128	| A slow ramp in | Hesitation, dawning | Long `rampIn` — **once per page**, it is close to feeling broken |
129	
130	Four rules follow:
131	
132	- **Silence must be authored, not left over.** *"An empty screen you meant
133	  reads as anticipation. An empty screen you did not mean reads as a page that
134	  failed to load, and the harness reports both as dead scroll."* If the empty
135	  viewport before the peak is deliberate, **say so in `BRIEF.md`** so the
136	  verification pass can tell it from dead scroll. This is the sentence that
137	  keeps `scroll_verify.py`'s `blankBands` check from being either useless or a
138	  false alarm.
139	- **Give the peak room.** The peak act has the largest span on the page by a
140	  visible margin. *"If every act is 2.2 vh, the page has no shape, whatever
141	  the curve in BRIEF.md says."*
142	- **Compress the administrative parts.** Specs, logistics, FAQ, credentials
143	  are information, not experience — flow sections at short stagger, never
144	  pinned acts with dwell. Spending scroll on them spends the visitor's
145	  patience on the part they will not remember.
146	- **A continuous world is the exception to pacing variety.** All of the above
147	  is about a page of *acts*. A worldflight is one camera move, and *"a camera
148	  that changes speed between legs reads as broken rather than as
149	  expressive."* There, hold one pace and let the peak carry the shape by being
150	  the single long leg — [`pace.md`](pace.md).
151	
152	The total-length budget stays **8–14 viewport-heights**. Pacing is how that
153	budget is spent, not permission to spend more: *"a page that needs 20 vh to
154	land its curve has too many acts, not too little room."*
155	
156	## The fingerprint gate
157	
158	Registry: `VAULT/wiki/projects/_index/design-fingerprints.md`, per-vault,
159	starting from whatever rows already exist — not repeating **yourself** across
160	builds, not a universal constraint. **Six dimensions**, recorded per row:
161	
162	| # | Dimension | What it records |
163	|---|---|---|
164	| 1 | Grammar | Which of `grammars.md`, or a named new one |
165	| 2 | Nav treatment | What the chrome is and what it's for |
166	| 3 | Hero device | What the first screen does |
167	| 4 | Act-sequence shape | Device order, act count, total viewport-heights |
168	| 5 | Close pattern | How the last screen behaves, what the CTA sits in |
169	| 6 | Signature move | The one bespoke interaction, in a phrase |
170	
171	**The gate: a new build must differ from EVERY existing row on at least 4 of
172	the 6** — four against each row individually, not averaged across the table.
173	Dimension 6 is free (unique by definition), so the gate really asks for 3
174	more out of the remaining 5 against each row. If the plan fails, **change
175	the plan, not the log** — rewriting a row to fit is what makes it worthless.
176	
177	**Row format** — one row per shipped build, all six dimensions plus a world
178	note and the path: `| Build | Grammar | Nav | Hero device | Act-sequence
179	shape | Close pattern | Signature move | Register | World / palette | Path |`
180	
181	**Rows are append-only.** From upstream `templates/FINGERPRINTS.md`:
182	
183	> *"A build that has been superseded stays in the table, because the space it
184	> occupies is still occupied."*
185	
186	A replaced, retired or rejected build keeps its row. The registry does not
187	record what is live; it records what surface has already been taken, and a
188	surface stays taken whether or not the build that claimed it is still up.
189	Deleting a row silently frees a shape for reuse, which is the same failure as
190	editing one to make room — *"never edit a row to make room for it. If a
191	planned build fails, change the plan."*
192	
193	**Fill every column.** A row with blanks cannot be scored 4-of-6 against, so
194	it weakens the gate for every build after it.
195	
196	**Keep a "what is taken" list beside the table.** Add a bullet whenever a
197	build claims something a later build should avoid reusing: a grammar, a nav
198	treatment, a close pattern, a signature move, an act-count-and-length band.
199	*"The shared columns are what the next build inherits as a constraint, so
200	writing them down is the whole point."*
201	
202	After shipping, append the row and say what it shares with prior rows — the
203	shared columns are exactly what the *next* build has to avoid.

| Short acts, hard cuts | Adrenaline, pulse, impatience | Acts under 1.4 vh, no `pin`, `dwell` at 0 |
| A long pin | Held breath, pressure, attention | `data-sc-span` 3+, overlapping cues, one idea |
| An empty viewport before a reveal | Silence before the drop | A ground-only act, no cue until the next one |
| A slow settle mid-act | The shot landing | `data-sc-dwell` 0.35–0.6, cue peak on the settle |
| A fast cue with a long plateau | Confidence, arrival | `data-sc-cue="0.1 0.9 0.08 0.4"` |
| A slow ramp in | Hesitation, dawning | Long `rampIn` — **once per page**, it is close to feeling broken |

Four rules follow:

- **Silence must be authored, not left over.** *"An empty screen you meant
  reads as anticipation. An empty screen you did not mean reads as a page that
  failed to load, and the harness reports both as dead scroll."* If the empty
  viewport before the peak is deliberate, **say so in `BRIEF.md`** so the
  verification pass can tell it from dead scroll. This is the sentence that
  keeps `scroll_verify.py`'s `blankBands` check from being either useless or a
  false alarm.
- **Give the peak room.** The peak act has the largest span on the page by a
  visible margin. *"If every act is 2.2 vh, the page has no shape, whatever
  the curve in BRIEF.md says."*
- **Compress the administrative parts.** Specs, logistics, FAQ, credentials
  are information, not experience — flow sections at short stagger, never
  pinned acts with dwell. Spending scroll on them spends the visitor's
  patience on the part they will not remember.
- **A continuous world is the exception to pacing variety.** All of the above
  is about a page of *acts*. A worldflight is one camera move, and *"a camera
  that changes speed between legs reads as broken rather than as
  expressive."* There, hold one pace and let the peak carry the shape by being
  the single long leg — [`pace.md`](pace.md).

The total-length budget stays **8–14 viewport-heights**. Pacing is how that
budget is spent, not permission to spend more: *"a page that needs 20 vh to
land its curve has too many acts, not too little room."*

## The fingerprint gate

Registry: `VAULT/wiki/projects/_index/design-fingerprints.md`, per-vault,
starting from whatever rows already exist — not repeating **yourself** across
builds, not a universal constraint. **Six dimensions**, recorded per row:

| # | Dimension | What it records |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Grammar | Which of `grammars.md`, or a named new one |
| 2 | Nav treatment | What the chrome is and what it's for |
| 3 | Hero device | What the first screen does |
| 4 | Act-sequence shape | Device order, act count, total viewport-heights |
| 5 | Close pattern | How the last screen behaves, what the CTA sits in |
| 6 | Signature move | The one bespoke interaction, in a phrase |

**The gate: a new build must differ from EVERY existing row on at least 4 of
the 6** — four against each row individually, not averaged across the table.
Dimension 6 is free (unique by definition), so the gate really asks for 3
more out of the remaining 5 against each row. If the plan fails, **change
the plan, not the log** — rewriting a row to fit is what makes it worthless.

**Row format** — one row per shipped build, all six dimensions plus a world
note and the path: `| Build | Grammar | Nav | Hero device | Act-sequence
shape | Close pattern | Signature move | Register | World / palette | Path |`

**Rows are append-only.** From upstream `templates/FINGERPRINTS.md`:

> *"A build that has been superseded stays in the table, because the space it
> occupies is still occupied."*

A replaced, retired or rejected build keeps its row. The registry does not
record what is live; it records what surface has already been taken, and a
surface stays taken whether or not the build that claimed it is still up.
Deleting a row silently frees a shape for reuse, which is the same failure as
editing one to make room — *"never edit a row to make room for it. If a
planned build fails, change the plan."*

**Fill every column.** A row with blanks cannot be scored 4-of-6 against, so
it weakens the gate for every build after it.

**Keep a "what is taken" list beside the table.** Add a bullet whenever a
build claims something a later build should avoid reusing: a grammar, a nav
treatment, a close pattern, a signature move, an act-count-and-length band.
*"The shared columns are what the next build inherits as a constraint, so
writing them down is the whole point."*

After shipping, append the row and say what it shares with prior rows — the
shared columns are exactly what the *next* build has to avoid.
