26	## The engine: GSAP + Lenis (house default from 2026-09-24)
27	
28	**Every new build animates with GSAP** (+ScrollTrigger, SplitText when text is
29	split) **and Lenis.** Scrollcraft (`scripts/scroll/`) stays only for pages already
30	built on it — do not port an existing scrollcraft page to GSAP+Lenis just because
31	it's the new default. **Never mix the two engines on one page**: two scroll owners
32	is two RAF loops fighting for the same frame. Anton's instruction: GSAP+Lenis for
33	all animations, applied wherever the motion fits the design and elements of each
34	page.
35	
36	**Linked, never installed or copied** (from 2026-10-02): the project reaches the
37	machine's global gsap 3.15.0 (all 25 modules) and lenis 1.3.26 through
38	`npm link gsap lenis`, done by `scripts/motion/link_motion.py`. The `design-intent`
39	hook runs it at the start of every design or animation job. It also scaffolds the
40	central `gsap.js` + `smooth-scroll.js`. Import maps, bundlers, trimming and deploy:
41	[`toolchain.md`](toolchain.md). `scripts/motion/vendor/` (4 files) is legacy and stays
42	only for pages already built on it (V3f, V3g). Never a CDN at runtime. GSAP 3.13+
43	including every plugin is free.
44	
45	The init, verbatim — house deviations from Lenis's own defaults, each explained
46	once here so no builder reads the Lenis README and takes the default instead:
47	
48	```js
49	var lenis = new Lenis({ autoRaf: false, anchors: true, respectReducedMotion: false, lerp: 0.075, wheelMultiplier: 0.6 });
50	window.__lenis = lenis;
51	gsap.ticker.add(function (time) { lenis.raf(time * 1000); });
52	gsap.ticker.lagSmoothing(500, 33);
53	lenis.on('scroll', ScrollTrigger.update);
54	```
55	
56	- **`respectReducedMotion: false`.** Lenis's own default is `true`, which would
57	  silently switch off all motion for Anton, whose Windows runs with animation
58	  effects off (house rule F-011 / CARL design decision 2026-09-07). Rörelse spelar
59	  alltid — motion always plays.
60	- **`anchors: true`.** Lenis's default is `false`, which breaks in-page anchor
61	  links silently — no error, they just stop scrolling to the target.
62	- **`autoRaf: false`, driven by `gsap.ticker`.** `gsap.ticker` is the only RAF
63	  driver on the page; Lenis's own rAF loop would be a second one racing it.
64	- **`gsap.ticker.lagSmoothing(500, 33)`, not `0`.** With `0`, one stalled frame (GC, a GPU queue, a
65	  first paint) hands Lenis the whole lost time at once and a running `scrollTo` jumps to catch
66	  up — measured Alunix V3g 2026-09-25: 490–724 px in a single frame after a click. With
67	  `(500, 33)` a stall over 500 ms counts as 33 ms: the scroll pauses and resumes (max step
68	  38–90 px over four runs). Lenis and ScrollTrigger share the same clamped clock, so they
69	  stay in sync.
70	- **`lenis.on('scroll', ScrollTrigger.update)`**
71	  keep GSAP's tab-blur catch-up off and ScrollTrigger's cached positions synced to
72	  Lenis's virtual scroll on every frame.
73	- **`window.__lenis`** is the dev hook every jump-test drives:
74	  `lenis.scrollTo(el, {immediate:true})`, never `window.scrollTo`.
75	
76	No `scrollerProxy` (Lenis scrolls the real page, not a virtual container). No CSS
77	`scroll-behavior: smooth` anywhere — it fights Lenis's own smoothing.
78	
79	**Iframes.** `lenis.css` sets `pointer-events: none` on iframes while smooth-scroll
80	is active — wanted behaviour for scroll-driven embeds (a showcase iframe the reader
81	scrolls *past*). For an embed the reader should scroll *inside*, set
82	`data-lenis-prevent` on it.
83	
84	### Scrollcraft device → GSAP equivalent
85	
86	| Scrollcraft | GSAP + Lenis |
87	|---|---|
88	| `scrub` (`data-sc-act=scrub`) | ScrollTrigger `scrub: true` timeline |
89	| `pin` | `pin: true`, created **once** at init |
90	| `pan` | pinned timeline, `xPercent` |
91	| `reveal` | `ScrollTrigger.batch` or a per-element trigger, fail toward visible |
92	| `kinetic` | SplitText `type:'lines,words,chars', mask:'lines'` + per-word `white-space: nowrap`; the mask needs `padding-bottom` with an equal negative margin so descenders survive |
93	| `parallax` | `yPercent` scrub |
94	| `count` | tween on a plain object + `snap` / `gsap.utils.snap` |
95	| `tilt` / `magnet` | `gsap.quickTo`, gated `(hover: hover)` |
96	| grid dissolve | `stagger: {grid, from:'random'}` |
97	| `responsive` (`gsap.matchMedia`) | `gsap.matchMedia()` |
98	
99	### Load-bearing rules
100	
101	- Create every ScrollTrigger **in page order.**
102	- **Never mix `scrub` and `toggleActions` on one trigger.**
103	- The **last element on the page** uses `end: 'bottom bottom'`.
104	- **With Lenis, use `scrub: true`, not a numeric scrub.** Lenis is the ONE
105	  smoothing layer on the page — a numeric scrub value stacks a second lag on top
106	  of it. Measured jank in V3f's showcase, 2026-09-24.
107	- **A pin is created once at init and is never killed/recreated on user
108	  interaction.** V3f's click handler did that and produced a hard, visible
109	  transition where the pin snapped instead of holding.
110	- **`end` is set in pixels via a function, with `invalidateOnRefresh: true` —
111	  never a `'+=Nvh'` string.** ScrollTrigger silently ignores the `vh` suffix on
112	  that shorthand — measured V3f R5.
113	
114	- **An iframe inside a pinned element needs an explicit `pinSpacer`.** ScrollTrigger re-parents
115	  the pinned element into its own pin-spacer on every `refresh()`, and a re-parented iframe
116	  reloads its document. If that iframe's `load` then asks for a refresh, the page runs a
117	  reload loop for the whole visit (measured Alunix V3f/V3g 2026-09-25: 6–12 reloads per
118	  iframe per pass, ~1/s, and the thesis headline two sections away lost half its frames).
119	  Put a wrapper in the markup (`<div class="x-pin-spacer"><div class="x-stage">…`) and pass
120	  `pinSpacer: '.x-pin-spacer'`. Never call `refresh()` from an iframe's `load`; an iframe
121	  has fixed dimensions and cannot change the outer layout.
122	- **Every scrubbed trigger uses `scrub: true`** — hero and thesis pins included, not only
123	  the one being edited this round. A numeric scrub anywhere is a second smoothing layer.
124	- **House pace (Anton 2026-09-25: "scrollen går för snabbt … man kastas förbi kortet").**
125	  Lenis `wheelMultiplier: 0.6` and `lerp: 0.075` — one wheel notch moves ~60 px and glides.
126	  A pin whose content the reader must watch happen (a card flip, a step change) spans at
127	  least 200 vh of scroll; nothing the reader should see may complete within one or two
128	  notches. Slower is only better if it stays even: verify with `section_probe.py`.
129	- **A timeline driven by `.progress(p)` must last exactly 1.** Tweens placed at absolute
130	  positions on a 0–1 scale end before 1, so the timeline is shorter and `progress(p)` runs
131	  it out of step with everything else driven by `p` — measured V3g 2026-09-25: late steps
132	  never faded in, and scrolling back left the active text at opacity 0. End every such
133	  timeline with `tl.set({}, {}, 1)`, and check a step by jumping to it AND by scrolling back
134	  to it, not only on the first forward pass.
135	- **Check: `scripts/section_probe.py URL --baseline <previous.json>`** after every round,
136	  on the WHOLE page, not only the edited section. It fails on an iframe that loads more
137	  than once, on any refresh during the scroll pass, and on any section whose p95 frame time
138	  got worse than the approved baseline. Verified to fail on V3f and V3g before the fix.
139	
140	### Skills to load before the first line of motion code
141	
142	In order: `lenis` → `gsap-core` → `gsap-scrolltrigger` → `gsap-timeline` →
143	`gsap-plugins` (if SplitText/Flip) → `gsap-performance` → `gsap-utils` (if
144	needed). Plus the UI-skills registry's `ibelick/fixing-motion-performance` — see
145	[`skill-orchestration.md`](../skill-orchestration.md).

147	## The cue contract — what verification actually catches you on
148	
149	`data-sc-cue="from [to [rampIn [rampOut]]]"`, all in act progress 0–1.
150	
151	| Form | Behaviour |
152	|---|---|
153	| `"0.2"` | fades in at 0.2, **holds to the end of the act** |
154	| `"0.1 0.6"` | in, plateau, out (ramps default 30% of window each) |
155	| `"0 0.78 0"` | **greet**: full opacity at act start, then fades — the hero form |
156	| `"0 1 0 0"` | **greet and hold**: full at p=0, no ramp either end |
157	
158	**The plateau is the point.** Without one, a cue is a triangle that touches full
159	opacity for a single instant, so the reader has to stop on exactly the right
160	pixel to see the line at full strength and every heading reads slightly faded.
161	`"0.1 0.9 0.15 0.4"` — fast in, long slow out — is the confident form. Cue
162	windows on a pinned act **overlap by design**, roughly 15% of the act: the
163	outgoing line is still fading while the next arrives, and a gap between cues
164	reads as a loading failure.
165	
166	Five rules, each one a real bug this fixture has caught:
167	
168	- **A hero cue needs the greet form.** A plain `"0 0.7"` means the first
169	  screen every visitor sees has no headline on it.
170	- **The last act's cue must hold** (one value). A two-value close cue fades
171	  the CTA out before the page ends.
172	- **Only the last act may hold.** A one-value cue on a *middle* pinned act
173	  stays lit through the whole un-pin slide — the line travels a full viewport
174	  up, crosses fixed chrome, overlaps the next section. Invisible until
175	  measured; shows up as a contrast failure nobody meant.
176	- **Ground or greet.** A pinned stage is fully visible ~1vh *before* its own
177	  progress leaves 0. A plain two-value first cue shows an empty stage for
178	  that whole travel — give the act a ground (image/colour already doing
179	  work) or open with a greet cue.
180	- **Clip time ≠ cue time.** A `scrub` clip is mapped across the stage's
181	  *entire visible life* (default), not across the pinned travel, because the
182	  stage is on screen for a viewport before the pin starts and after it ends.
183	  Cues keep using `p` (they belong to the pin); the clip uses a separately
184	  computed `vp`. Reaching for `data-sc-clip-map="travel"` reintroduces the
185	  freeze — there's almost no reason to.
186	
187	Two more that a harness will not catch by itself:
188	
189	- **Pan overflow must be measured, not assumed.** The rail travels exactly
190	  `scrollWidth - viewport`; a rail narrower than the viewport travels **zero**
191	  and the act reads as a still. `rail.scrollWidth - innerWidth` — check it,
192	  don't guess.
193	- **Parallax rate is hundreds of pixels total, not a viewport fraction** — see
194	  the table above. A rate of 0.35 across three viewport-heights of scroll is
195	  35px: invisible.
196	
197	Composing an act: devices stack (a pinned stage can hold a scrub clip, a
198	parallax layer, a kinetic headline, a spotlight at once), but one thing is the
199	reason the act exists — say that thing in one sentence or the act has none.
200	
201	## The playhead is lerped (§1)
202	
203	The mechanism the whole kit's smoothness rests on, and the one F-012 kept
204	being blamed on. **Scroll never writes `currentTime`.** It writes a *target*,
205	and a standalone rAF loop walks the clip toward that target at a fixed
206	fraction per frame:
207	
208	> *"Wheel events do not arrive at a constant rate, so a 1:1 write reproduces
209	> every gap in them and the clip reads as a stutter rather than a glide."*
210	
211	Three mechanisms, all on by default:
212	
213	- **Lerp 0.18 per frame.** `data-sc-lerp` overrides it, on the mount root for
214	  the whole page or on a single `<video>`. **Clamped to 0.02–1 and never read
215	  as 0** — a 0 lerp is a playhead that never moves. Reach for an override only
216	  when a page's clips are short enough that 0.18 visibly lags the hand.
217	  Worldflight wants 0.12 instead; see [`pace.md`](pace.md).
218	- **Deadband: 8 ms desktop, 20 ms mobile.** A write smaller than that costs a
219	  seek and shows nothing; on a phone it costs more than it shows.
220	- **Seek coalescing.** No seek is queued while the decoder is still resolving
221	  the last one. *"A fast flick otherwise piles seeks up and freezes the clip."*
222	
223	An offscreen clip that has already reached its target stops being touched at
224	all. (Upstream states the offscreen skip without a threshold value; the 0.002
225	figure belongs to `shoot.mjs`'s settle test, below, not to this skip.)
226	
227	This applies to **every** scrub clip on the page, act or worldflight. It is
228	also why the shooter waits for the playhead to arrive before each frame:
229	
230	> *"A frame captured mid-lerp is a frame the page never actually holds."*
231	
232	`shoot.mjs` settles on `|current − target| < 0.002 && !seeking`. Any harness
233	the chain runs against a scrubbed page inherits that requirement — a
234	screenshot taken mid-lerp makes the run unrepeatable, not merely imprecise.
235	
236	Upstream also drops the damping to 1.0 (no smoothing at all) under reduced
237	motion. **That branch does not port: F-011.** The lerp is unconditional here,
238	which is the correct behaviour anyway — it is a smoothing mechanism, not an
239	effect, and turning it off is what produces the stepping fault.
240	
241	## Layered scenes: where the premium feel comes from (§6)
242	
243	Ported from `devices.md` § 6, measured off a reference premium site and proven
244	on a live build. A flat page moves as one sheet; a layered page is a stack of
245	cut-out planes sliding past each other, and *"the eye reads that differential
246	motion as depth before it reads anything else."* It is the single biggest
247	difference between a page that feels built and one that feels assembled, and
248	it costs three transparent images and a multiplier each.
249	
250	- **Plan the planes back to front.** Far ridge, mid ridge, the product, then a
251	  **foreground plane in front of the product**. The product sits between mid
252	  and front, so the foreground overtakes it as the reader scrolls. That
253	  overtaking is the move.
254	- **Small rate differences, not big ones.** The reference hero lags the far
255	  plane **31%** behind the page, the mid plane **17%**, the product **20%**,
256	  and foreground and copy travel at exactly **1×**. Adjacent planes differ by
257	  **10–30%**. Larger stops reading as distance and starts reading as things
258	  sliding around. **Copy always rides at 1×.**
259	- **Shape the foreground for the product.** A straight-edged foreground covers
260	  the product's CTA within a few hundred pixels of scroll. Cut it so it dips
261	  where the product is and rises at the edges, and the button stays in view
262	  two to three times as long.
263	- **Every plane is solid below its silhouette.** Cut-out art that fades to
264	  transparent at the bottom lets the plane behind show through as the planes
265	  separate. Fill each column solid from its first opaque pixel down.
266	- **Fade the section floor.** Planes travel past the section's bottom edge and
267	  are clipped there. A gradient to the page ground over the last 200–300 px,
268	  layered above every plane, hides the clip line at any scroll position.
269	
270	Three traps, each of which cost a round of fixes:
271	
272	- A global `img { max-width: 100% }` shrinks an absolutely positioned plane to
273	  the viewport on phones, so the far layer never shows. **Planes carry
274	  `max-width: none` and a fixed pixel width.**
275	- **Never `transition: transform` on a parallaxed element.** A reveal class is
276	  the usual culprit. The transition eases every per-frame scroll write over
277	  its own duration, and on a phone that reads as the product lagging a full
278	  second behind the thumb. Parallaxed elements transition **opacity only**.
279	- Replacing a plane's art under the same filename ships nothing to a phone
280	  holding the old bytes. **New art gets a new name.**
281	
282	`data-sc-parallax` and a raw scroll multiplier are the same tool in different
283	units. What matters is the **ratio between planes**, not the absolute travel.
284	
285	## The premium fade-in, exactly (§8)
286	
287	The `flow` + `in` device is most of the page, so its defaults decide how the
288	page feels between the acts:
289	
290	| Ingredient | Value |
291	|---|---|
292	| Opacity | 0 → 1 |
293	| Rise | **~14 px** |
294	| Duration | **~620 ms**, ease-out |
295	| Stagger | **30–80 ms**, children in reading order |
296	| Trigger | IntersectionObserver, `-12%` bottom root margin, **fires once** |
297	
298	- **A fade with no rise reads as a loading glitch.** A rise **past 24 px reads
299	  as a slide.** 14 px is the band, not a starting point to tune upward.
300	- The `-12%` margin fires the reveal when the reader is looking, not when the
301	  first pixel clears the fold.
302	- `data-sc-in` is what the engine watches. Without it nothing fires and the
303	  stagger children stay hidden.
304	- **Content that re-hides on the way back up is a defect, not an effect.**
305	- *"Larger, slower, or bouncier is never more premium; the restraint is the
306	  signal."*
307	
308	**A flow section directly after a pinned act takes reduced padding.** The
309	pinned stage needs a full viewport to scroll off, and full `--sc-section`
310	padding on top of that delays the flow section's first content by another
311	screen. The harness will not call it dead scroll — correctly, the stage is
312	moving — and the reader still sees a near-empty screen. Cut the block padding
313	there and start the first reveal near `p = 0`.
314	
315	## Rail settle on `pan` (§3)
316	
317	Lateral travel alone reads as a slideshow on rails. **Give the rail's items a
318	staggered settle driven from `--sc-p`** and they read as a drawer being
319	pulled instead.
320	
321	- **Exempt the first item** — a `pan` act needs its opening content already
322	  present.
323	- **Floor the opacity around 0.55**, so a not-yet-settled card reads as
324	  arriving rather than as failing to load.
325	
326	Upstream gates the settle to `prefers-reduced-motion` — **utgår, F-011**.
327	The settle always runs. What *does* survive from
328	the same passage is the reachability requirement, which is not a motion
329	preference at all: a `pan` rail's transform **is** the navigation, so nothing
330	may zero it and park the act on its first screenful. Every item in a rail
331	stays reachable, and that is checked on the sheet, not assumed.
332	
333	Two more, from the same section:
334	
335	- **Card copy is read while cropped.** Items enter and leave through the
336	  viewport edges, so a heading is half-shown for most of its life, and two
337	  half-headings side by side can read as a third word (`TRACE` beside
338	  `EVALUATE` becoming `RE EVALUATE`). Keep card headings to one or two short
339	  words and expect every line to be read partially cut off.
340	- If three items do not reach half a viewport of overflow, **the fix is more
341	  rail, not wider cards**: put the act's heading in as the first item and a
342	  closing note as the last. Both earn their place, and they add the width the
343	  travel needs.
344	
345	## Devices that cannot share an element (§9)
346	
347	**`magnet`, `parallax` and `cue` all write `transform`.** The magnet writes
348	every frame in its own rAF loop, so it silently wins and the cue's entrance
349	rise is discarded — a visible animation lost to a race, with nothing in the
350	console.
351	
352	- On a magnetic CTA, set **`data-sc-rise="0"`** so the cue writes a no-op
353	  instead of losing to the magnet.
354	- A cued element that wants its own continuous transform drives an **inner
355	  wrapper** from `--sc-p` in CSS, rather than stacking a second device on the
356	  same node.
357	
358	All three pointer devices **interpolate toward** the pointer rather than
359	tracking it directly: *"direct tracking reads as artificial because it carries
360	no momentum."* They stay gated to `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` so
361	touch never fires a false hover — that gate is a pointer-capability query, not
362	a motion preference, and it stands.
363	The reduced-motion half of the same sentence does not port (F-011).
364	
365	## Kinetic type: the mask and the re-split (§5)
366	
367	Each unit slides up from **behind a mask**, so it enters from a clean edge
368	rather than simply fading.
369	
370	- **Line masks must reserve room for descenders.** A mask clipped to the line
371	  box shears the tails off g, y, p and j, *"and that is the single most common
372	  way this effect looks broken."*
373	- **Line splitting measures real line boxes, so it re-runs after
374	  `document.fonts.ready`.** Do not call it on text still loading its face. The
375	  same `fonts.ready` handle earns its place twice over: a webfont swapping in
376	  changes the measured height of every copy block, so anything sized against
377	  those blocks (a scrim plate, a rail) is wrong until it re-measures.
378	- Lines are almost always right; words for a short punch line; characters
379	  approximately never, *"because it turns reading into waiting."*
380	- **One kinetic headline per act, at most.**
381	
382	## What makes a `count` land (§7)
383	
384	- **Ease out, hard.** A cubic ease-out, so most of the distance goes by in the
385	  first third and the last digits settle slowly. *"A linear count reads as a
386	  slot machine."*
387	- **1.2–1.8 s.** Under a second and the reader misses that it moved; past two
388	  and they are waiting for a number they have already guessed.
389	- **Fires at half visibility, once**, so the reader is looking at it when it
390	  starts, and it never re-runs on the way back up.
391	- **Pair it with the fade.** A counter inside a `data-sc-in` stack rises in
392	  with its label and starts ticking as it arrives — *"the same numbers static
393	  on the page read as a spreadsheet."*
394	- Write the target exactly as it should render, commas included; the engine
395	  strips them before parsing and applies `tabular-nums` so the layout does not
396	  jitter.
397	
398	**A concept, fictional or pre-launch brand has no verified figures, so it has
399	no counters.** The device suits a SaaS or agency page and will look good in
400	the score table, *"which is exactly the trap: every number you could put in it
401	would be invented."* Decide this before designing an act around a number, not
402	after. Real brand, real stats, or a different device.
403	
404	## Appendix: pattern vocabulary
405	
406	Named patterns from taste-skill § 10, carried here so orchestrator, builder
407	and reviewer name the same thing. It is a **vocabulary, not a menu** — several
408	entries below are banned as directions elsewhere in the chain (glassmorphism,
409	holographic foil, carousels, gooey menus) and appear here only so a critique
410	can say which trope it is refusing.
411	
412	- **Hero** — Asymmetric Split · Editorial Manifesto · Video/Media Mask ·
413	  Kinetic-Type · Curtain-Reveal · Scroll-Pinned.
414	- **Nav** — Dock Magnification · Magnetic Button (`data-sc-magnet`) · Gooey
415	  Menu · Dynamic Island · Contextual Radial · Floating Speed Dial · Mega Menu
416	  Reveal.
417	- **Layout** — Bento Grid · Masonry · Chroma Grid · Split-Screen Scroll ·
418	  Sticky-Stack Sections.
419	- **Cards** — Parallax Tilt Card (`data-sc-tilt`) · Spotlight Border Card
420	  (`data-sc-spotlight`) · Glassmorphism Panel · Holographic Foil ·
421	  Tinder Swipe Stack · Morphing Modal.
422	- **Scroll** — Sticky Scroll Stack · Horizontal Scroll Hijack (= `pan`) ·
423	  Locomotive / Sequence Scroll (= `scrub`) · Zoom Parallax · Scroll Progress
424	  Path · Liquid Swipe Transition.
425	- **Galleries** — Dome Gallery · Coverflow Carousel · Drag-to-Pan Grid ·
426	  Accordion Image Slider · Hover Image Trail · Glitch Effect Image.
427	- **Type** — Kinetic Marquee · **Text Mask Reveal** (massive type as a
428	  transparent window onto video — this is K2's letter-window) · Text Scramble
429	  · Circular Text Path · Gradient Stroke Animation · Kinetic Typography Grid.
430	- **Micro** — Particle Explosion Button · Liquid Pull-to-Refresh · Skeleton
431	  Shimmer · Directional Hover-Aware Button · Ripple Click · Animated SVG Line
432	  Drawing · Mesh Gradient Background · Lens Blur Depth.
433	
434	Names alone are not permission. A pattern still has to clear the fingerprint
435	gate, the register, and `../motion.md` before it ships.
436	
437	## Never restyle the engine's classes (AB06, 2026-09-03)
438	
439	Theme the engine only through its six colour tokens and two fonts. A project rule on
440	`.sc-stage`, `.sc-copy`, `.sc-scrim` or any other `.sc-*` class silently wins over the
441	engine: the console then says `[scrollcraft] act "…" will not pin: its stage computes
442	position:relative` and every pinned act scrolls away, leaving its spacer as dead scroll.
443	Read the console for `[scrollcraft]` warnings before anything else in Step 5, and run
444	`scripts/scroll_verify.py` — a blind one-shot cannot see either. The engine is opt-in per
445	grammar (scrub, pin, pan); a page that keeps the chain's own single set-piece + shared
446	reveal does not need it.
447

# The device kit, condensed

Nine ways scroll can drive the page. Pick per beat, never per page: ≥4 device
families, never the same one twice running. Every act publishes `--sc-p` (0–1)
on itself, so bespoke CSS can ride the same value the kit devices use. Full
depth, worked examples, and every trap: `upstream/scroll-craft/.../references/devices.md`.

| # | Device | Syntax | Span / rate | One-line rule |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `scrub` | `data-sc-act="scrub" data-sc-span="2.6" data-sc-dwell="0.35"` on the section; `data-sc-scrub data-sc-src="…"` on the `<video>` | span 2.2–3.0 for a hero | ≤2 per page. The wheel scrubs a pre-rendered clip; spend it on the open |
| 2 | `pin` | `data-sc-act="pin" data-sc-span="3"` | span ≥1.2 (below that, progress jumps 0→1 in one notch) | The frame holds, copy states cross over inside it |
| 3 | `pan` | `data-sc-act="pan" data-sc-span="3.2"`; rail gets `data-sc-pan="0.08"` | ~1vh per item + 1 | Lateral = breadth, not hierarchy. Overflow must be measured, not assumed |
| 4 | `reveal` | `data-sc-reveal="up|down|left|right|iris" data-sc-reveal-at="0.15 0.55"` | — | `clip-path` wipe = change of state. `iris` once per page at most |
| 5 | `kinetic` | `data-sc-kinetic="lines|words|chars"` on a cued heading | — | Lines almost always right, chars ~never. One kinetic headline per act |
| 6 | `parallax` | `data-sc-parallax="-0.6"` | rate is **hundreds of px total travel**, not a fraction — usable range 0.3–1.5 (framed), 1–2 (full-bleed) | Never on body copy. 3 layers is plenty |
| 7 | `count` | `data-sc-count="0 4,200" data-sc-count-at="0.1 0.5"` | 1.2–1.8s outside an act (`data-sc-count-ms`) | Only real numbers. No verified figure, no counter |
| 8 | `flow` + `in` | `data-sc-in data-sc-stagger="70"` on the wrap | stagger 30–80ms | The rest of the page. Fires once, opacity+14px rise, ~620ms ease-out |
| 9 | pointer: `tilt` / `magnet` / `spotlight` | `data-sc-tilt="7"` (5–9°), `data-sc-magnet="0.28"` (0.2–0.35, CTA only), `data-sc-spotlight` (publishes `--sc-mx`/`--sc-my`) | — | Gated to `(hover:hover) and (pointer:fine)`. Never gated on reduced motion (F-011, superseded 2026-09-07) |

`drift` (`data-sc-drift="#0A0806"` on an act) is not a device, it's a
property: the page ground interpolates toward it while the act is live. 3–5
stops, one theme family. On a page of many *short* acts several can be
part-way through at once — paint grounds per section instead of drifting; see
upstream §10.

## The engine: GSAP + Lenis (house default from 2026-09-24)

**Every new build animates with GSAP** (+ScrollTrigger, SplitText when text is
split) **and Lenis.** Scrollcraft (`scripts/scroll/`) stays only for pages already
built on it — do not port an existing scrollcraft page to GSAP+Lenis just because
it's the new default. **Never mix the two engines on one page**: two scroll owners
is two RAF loops fighting for the same frame. Anton's instruction: GSAP+Lenis for
all animations, applied wherever the motion fits the design and elements of each
page.

**Linked, never installed or copied** (from 2026-10-02): the project reaches the
machine's global gsap 3.15.0 (all 25 modules) and lenis 1.3.26 through
`npm link gsap lenis`, done by `scripts/motion/link_motion.py`. The `design-intent`
hook runs it at the start of every design or animation job. It also scaffolds the
central `gsap.js` + `smooth-scroll.js`. Import maps, bundlers, trimming and deploy:
[`toolchain.md`](toolchain.md). `scripts/motion/vendor/` (4 files) is legacy and stays
only for pages already built on it (V3f, V3g). Never a CDN at runtime. GSAP 3.13+
including every plugin is free.

The init, verbatim — house deviations from Lenis's own defaults, each explained
once here so no builder reads the Lenis README and takes the default instead:

```js
var lenis = new Lenis({ autoRaf: false, anchors: true, respectReducedMotion: false, lerp: 0.075, wheelMultiplier: 0.6 });
window.__lenis = lenis;
gsap.ticker.add(function (time) { lenis.raf(time * 1000); });
gsap.ticker.lagSmoothing(500, 33);
lenis.on('scroll', ScrollTrigger.update);
```

- **`respectReducedMotion: false`.** Lenis's own default is `true`, which would
  silently switch off all motion for Anton, whose Windows runs with animation
  effects off (house rule F-011 / CARL design decision 2026-09-07). Rörelse spelar
  alltid — motion always plays.
- **`anchors: true`.** Lenis's default is `false`, which breaks in-page anchor
  links silently — no error, they just stop scrolling to the target.
- **`autoRaf: false`, driven by `gsap.ticker`.** `gsap.ticker` is the only RAF
  driver on the page; Lenis's own rAF loop would be a second one racing it.
- **`gsap.ticker.lagSmoothing(500, 33)`, not `0`.** With `0`, one stalled frame (GC, a GPU queue, a
  first paint) hands Lenis the whole lost time at once and a running `scrollTo` jumps to catch
  up — measured Alunix V3g 2026-09-25: 490–724 px in a single frame after a click. With
  `(500, 33)` a stall over 500 ms counts as 33 ms: the scroll pauses and resumes (max step
  38–90 px over four runs). Lenis and ScrollTrigger share the same clamped clock, so they
  stay in sync.
- **`lenis.on('scroll', ScrollTrigger.update)`**
  keep GSAP's tab-blur catch-up off and ScrollTrigger's cached positions synced to
  Lenis's virtual scroll on every frame.
- **`window.__lenis`** is the dev hook every jump-test drives:
  `lenis.scrollTo(el, {immediate:true})`, never `window.scrollTo`.

No `scrollerProxy` (Lenis scrolls the real page, not a virtual container). No CSS
`scroll-behavior: smooth` anywhere — it fights Lenis's own smoothing.

**Iframes.** `lenis.css` sets `pointer-events: none` on iframes while smooth-scroll
is active — wanted behaviour for scroll-driven embeds (a showcase iframe the reader
scrolls *past*). For an embed the reader should scroll *inside*, set
`data-lenis-prevent` on it.

### Scrollcraft device → GSAP equivalent

| Scrollcraft | GSAP + Lenis |
|---|---|
| `scrub` (`data-sc-act=scrub`) | ScrollTrigger `scrub: true` timeline |
| `pin` | `pin: true`, created **once** at init |
| `pan` | pinned timeline, `xPercent` |
| `reveal` | `ScrollTrigger.batch` or a per-element trigger, fail toward visible |
| `kinetic` | SplitText `type:'lines,words,chars', mask:'lines'` + per-word `white-space: nowrap`; the mask needs `padding-bottom` with an equal negative margin so descenders survive |
| `parallax` | `yPercent` scrub |
| `count` | tween on a plain object + `snap` / `gsap.utils.snap` |
| `tilt` / `magnet` | `gsap.quickTo`, gated `(hover: hover)` |
| grid dissolve | `stagger: {grid, from:'random'}` |
| `responsive` (`gsap.matchMedia`) | `gsap.matchMedia()` |

### Load-bearing rules

- Create every ScrollTrigger **in page order.**
- **Never mix `scrub` and `toggleActions` on one trigger.**
- The **last element on the page** uses `end: 'bottom bottom'`.
- **With Lenis, use `scrub: true`, not a numeric scrub.** Lenis is the ONE
  smoothing layer on the page — a numeric scrub value stacks a second lag on top
  of it. Measured jank in V3f's showcase, 2026-09-24.
- **A pin is created once at init and is never killed/recreated on user
  interaction.** V3f's click handler did that and produced a hard, visible
  transition where the pin snapped instead of holding.
- **`end` is set in pixels via a function, with `invalidateOnRefresh: true` —
  never a `'+=Nvh'` string.** ScrollTrigger silently ignores the `vh` suffix on
  that shorthand — measured V3f R5.

- **An iframe inside a pinned element needs an explicit `pinSpacer`.** ScrollTrigger re-parents
  the pinned element into its own pin-spacer on every `refresh()`, and a re-parented iframe
  reloads its document. If that iframe's `load` then asks for a refresh, the page runs a
  reload loop for the whole visit (measured Alunix V3f/V3g 2026-09-25: 6–12 reloads per
  iframe per pass, ~1/s, and the thesis headline two sections away lost half its frames).
  Put a wrapper in the markup (`<div class="x-pin-spacer"><div class="x-stage">…`) and pass
  `pinSpacer: '.x-pin-spacer'`. Never call `refresh()` from an iframe's `load`; an iframe
  has fixed dimensions and cannot change the outer layout.
- **Every scrubbed trigger uses `scrub: true`** — hero and thesis pins included, not only
  the one being edited this round. A numeric scrub anywhere is a second smoothing layer.
- **House pace (Anton 2026-09-25: "scrollen går för snabbt … man kastas förbi kortet").**
  Lenis `wheelMultiplier: 0.6` and `lerp: 0.075` — one wheel notch moves ~60 px and glides.
  A pin whose content the reader must watch happen (a card flip, a step change) spans at
  least 200 vh of scroll; nothing the reader should see may complete within one or two
  notches. Slower is only better if it stays even: verify with `section_probe.py`.
- **A timeline driven by `.progress(p)` must last exactly 1.** Tweens placed at absolute
  positions on a 0–1 scale end before 1, so the timeline is shorter and `progress(p)` runs
  it out of step with everything else driven by `p` — measured V3g 2026-09-25: late steps
  never faded in, and scrolling back left the active text at opacity 0. End every such
  timeline with `tl.set({}, {}, 1)`, and check a step by jumping to it AND by scrolling back
  to it, not only on the first forward pass.
- **Check: `scripts/section_probe.py URL --baseline <previous.json>`** after every round,
  on the WHOLE page, not only the edited section. It fails on an iframe that loads more
  than once, on any refresh during the scroll pass, and on any section whose p95 frame time
  got worse than the approved baseline. Verified to fail on V3f and V3g before the fix.

### Skills to load before the first line of motion code

In order: `lenis` → `gsap-core` → `gsap-scrolltrigger` → `gsap-timeline` →
`gsap-plugins` (if SplitText/Flip) → `gsap-performance` → `gsap-utils` (if
needed). Plus the UI-skills registry's `ibelick/fixing-motion-performance` — see
[`skill-orchestration.md`](../skill-orchestration.md).

## The cue contract — what verification actually catches you on

`data-sc-cue="from [to [rampIn [rampOut]]]"`, all in act progress 0–1.

| Form | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `"0.2"` | fades in at 0.2, **holds to the end of the act** |
| `"0.1 0.6"` | in, plateau, out (ramps default 30% of window each) |
| `"0 0.78 0"` | **greet**: full opacity at act start, then fades — the hero form |
| `"0 1 0 0"` | **greet and hold**: full at p=0, no ramp either end |

**The plateau is the point.** Without one, a cue is a triangle that touches full
opacity for a single instant, so the reader has to stop on exactly the right
pixel to see the line at full strength and every heading reads slightly faded.
`"0.1 0.9 0.15 0.4"` — fast in, long slow out — is the confident form. Cue
windows on a pinned act **overlap by design**, roughly 15% of the act: the
outgoing line is still fading while the next arrives, and a gap between cues
reads as a loading failure.

Five rules, each one a real bug this fixture has caught:

- **A hero cue needs the greet form.** A plain `"0 0.7"` means the first
  screen every visitor sees has no headline on it.
- **The last act's cue must hold** (one value). A two-value close cue fades
  the CTA out before the page ends.
- **Only the last act may hold.** A one-value cue on a *middle* pinned act
  stays lit through the whole un-pin slide — the line travels a full viewport
  up, crosses fixed chrome, overlaps the next section. Invisible until
  measured; shows up as a contrast failure nobody meant.
- **Ground or greet.** A pinned stage is fully visible ~1vh *before* its own
  progress leaves 0. A plain two-value first cue shows an empty stage for
  that whole travel — give the act a ground (image/colour already doing
  work) or open with a greet cue.
- **Clip time ≠ cue time.** A `scrub` clip is mapped across the stage's
  *entire visible life* (default), not across the pinned travel, because the
  stage is on screen for a viewport before the pin starts and after it ends.
  Cues keep using `p` (they belong to the pin); the clip uses a separately
  computed `vp`. Reaching for `data-sc-clip-map="travel"` reintroduces the
  freeze — there's almost no reason to.

Two more that a harness will not catch by itself:

- **Pan overflow must be measured, not assumed.** The rail travels exactly
  `scrollWidth - viewport`; a rail narrower than the viewport travels **zero**
  and the act reads as a still. `rail.scrollWidth - innerWidth` — check it,
  don't guess.
- **Parallax rate is hundreds of pixels total, not a viewport fraction** — see
  the table above. A rate of 0.35 across three viewport-heights of scroll is
  35px: invisible.

Composing an act: devices stack (a pinned stage can hold a scrub clip, a
parallax layer, a kinetic headline, a spotlight at once), but one thing is the
reason the act exists — say that thing in one sentence or the act has none.

## The playhead is lerped (§1)

The mechanism the whole kit's smoothness rests on, and the one F-012 kept
being blamed on. **Scroll never writes `currentTime`.** It writes a *target*,
and a standalone rAF loop walks the clip toward that target at a fixed
fraction per frame:

> *"Wheel events do not arrive at a constant rate, so a 1:1 write reproduces
> every gap in them and the clip reads as a stutter rather than a glide."*

Three mechanisms, all on by default:

- **Lerp 0.18 per frame.** `data-sc-lerp` overrides it, on the mount root for
  the whole page or on a single `<video>`. **Clamped to 0.02–1 and never read
  as 0** — a 0 lerp is a playhead that never moves. Reach for an override only
  when a page's clips are short enough that 0.18 visibly lags the hand.
  Worldflight wants 0.12 instead; see [`pace.md`](pace.md).
- **Deadband: 8 ms desktop, 20 ms mobile.** A write smaller than that costs a
  seek and shows nothing; on a phone it costs more than it shows.
- **Seek coalescing.** No seek is queued while the decoder is still resolving
  the last one. *"A fast flick otherwise piles seeks up and freezes the clip."*

An offscreen clip that has already reached its target stops being touched at
all. (Upstream states the offscreen skip without a threshold value; the 0.002
figure belongs to `shoot.mjs`'s settle test, below, not to this skip.)

This applies to **every** scrub clip on the page, act or worldflight. It is
also why the shooter waits for the playhead to arrive before each frame:

> *"A frame captured mid-lerp is a frame the page never actually holds."*

`shoot.mjs` settles on `|current − target| < 0.002 && !seeking`. Any harness
the chain runs against a scrubbed page inherits that requirement — a
screenshot taken mid-lerp makes the run unrepeatable, not merely imprecise.

Upstream also drops the damping to 1.0 (no smoothing at all) under reduced
motion. **That branch does not port: F-011.** The lerp is unconditional here,
which is the correct behaviour anyway — it is a smoothing mechanism, not an
effect, and turning it off is what produces the stepping fault.

## Layered scenes: where the premium feel comes from (§6)

Ported from `devices.md` § 6, measured off a reference premium site and proven
on a live build. A flat page moves as one sheet; a layered page is a stack of
cut-out planes sliding past each other, and *"the eye reads that differential
motion as depth before it reads anything else."* It is the single biggest
difference between a page that feels built and one that feels assembled, and
it costs three transparent images and a multiplier each.

- **Plan the planes back to front.** Far ridge, mid ridge, the product, then a
  **foreground plane in front of the product**. The product sits between mid
  and front, so the foreground overtakes it as the reader scrolls. That
  overtaking is the move.
- **Small rate differences, not big ones.** The reference hero lags the far
  plane **31%** behind the page, the mid plane **17%**, the product **20%**,
  and foreground and copy travel at exactly **1×**. Adjacent planes differ by
  **10–30%**. Larger stops reading as distance and starts reading as things
  sliding around. **Copy always rides at 1×.**
- **Shape the foreground for the product.** A straight-edged foreground covers
  the product's CTA within a few hundred pixels of scroll. Cut it so it dips
  where the product is and rises at the edges, and the button stays in view
  two to three times as long.
- **Every plane is solid below its silhouette.** Cut-out art that fades to
  transparent at the bottom lets the plane behind show through as the planes
  separate. Fill each column solid from its first opaque pixel down.
- **Fade the section floor.** Planes travel past the section's bottom edge and
  are clipped there. A gradient to the page ground over the last 200–300 px,
  layered above every plane, hides the clip line at any scroll position.

Three traps, each of which cost a round of fixes:

- A global `img { max-width: 100% }` shrinks an absolutely positioned plane to
  the viewport on phones, so the far layer never shows. **Planes carry
  `max-width: none` and a fixed pixel width.**
- **Never `transition: transform` on a parallaxed element.** A reveal class is
  the usual culprit. The transition eases every per-frame scroll write over
  its own duration, and on a phone that reads as the product lagging a full
  second behind the thumb. Parallaxed elements transition **opacity only**.
- Replacing a plane's art under the same filename ships nothing to a phone
  holding the old bytes. **New art gets a new name.**

`data-sc-parallax` and a raw scroll multiplier are the same tool in different
units. What matters is the **ratio between planes**, not the absolute travel.

## The premium fade-in, exactly (§8)

The `flow` + `in` device is most of the page, so its defaults decide how the
page feels between the acts:

| Ingredient | Value |
|---|---|
| Opacity | 0 → 1 |
| Rise | **~14 px** |
| Duration | **~620 ms**, ease-out |
| Stagger | **30–80 ms**, children in reading order |
| Trigger | IntersectionObserver, `-12%` bottom root margin, **fires once** |

- **A fade with no rise reads as a loading glitch.** A rise **past 24 px reads
  as a slide.** 14 px is the band, not a starting point to tune upward.
- The `-12%` margin fires the reveal when the reader is looking, not when the
  first pixel clears the fold.
- `data-sc-in` is what the engine watches. Without it nothing fires and the
  stagger children stay hidden.
- **Content that re-hides on the way back up is a defect, not an effect.**
- *"Larger, slower, or bouncier is never more premium; the restraint is the
  signal."*

**A flow section directly after a pinned act takes reduced padding.** The
pinned stage needs a full viewport to scroll off, and full `--sc-section`
padding on top of that delays the flow section's first content by another
screen. The harness will not call it dead scroll — correctly, the stage is
moving — and the reader still sees a near-empty screen. Cut the block padding
there and start the first reveal near `p = 0`.

## Rail settle on `pan` (§3)

Lateral travel alone reads as a slideshow on rails. **Give the rail's items a
staggered settle driven from `--sc-p`** and they read as a drawer being
pulled instead.

- **Exempt the first item** — a `pan` act needs its opening content already
  present.
- **Floor the opacity around 0.55**, so a not-yet-settled card reads as
  arriving rather than as failing to load.

Upstream gates the settle to `prefers-reduced-motion` — **utgår, F-011**.
The settle always runs. What *does* survive from
the same passage is the reachability requirement, which is not a motion
preference at all: a `pan` rail's transform **is** the navigation, so nothing
may zero it and park the act on its first screenful. Every item in a rail
stays reachable, and that is checked on the sheet, not assumed.

Two more, from the same section:

- **Card copy is read while cropped.** Items enter and leave through the
  viewport edges, so a heading is half-shown for most of its life, and two
  half-headings side by side can read as a third word (`TRACE` beside
  `EVALUATE` becoming `RE EVALUATE`). Keep card headings to one or two short
  words and expect every line to be read partially cut off.
- If three items do not reach half a viewport of overflow, **the fix is more
  rail, not wider cards**: put the act's heading in as the first item and a
  closing note as the last. Both earn their place, and they add the width the
  travel needs.

## Devices that cannot share an element (§9)

**`magnet`, `parallax` and `cue` all write `transform`.** The magnet writes
every frame in its own rAF loop, so it silently wins and the cue's entrance
rise is discarded — a visible animation lost to a race, with nothing in the
console.

- On a magnetic CTA, set **`data-sc-rise="0"`** so the cue writes a no-op
  instead of losing to the magnet.
- A cued element that wants its own continuous transform drives an **inner
  wrapper** from `--sc-p` in CSS, rather than stacking a second device on the
  same node.

All three pointer devices **interpolate toward** the pointer rather than
tracking it directly: *"direct tracking reads as artificial because it carries
no momentum."* They stay gated to `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` so
touch never fires a false hover — that gate is a pointer-capability query, not
a motion preference, and it stands.
The reduced-motion half of the same sentence does not port (F-011).

## Kinetic type: the mask and the re-split (§5)

Each unit slides up from **behind a mask**, so it enters from a clean edge
rather than simply fading.

- **Line masks must reserve room for descenders.** A mask clipped to the line
  box shears the tails off g, y, p and j, *"and that is the single most common
  way this effect looks broken."*
- **Line splitting measures real line boxes, so it re-runs after
  `document.fonts.ready`.** Do not call it on text still loading its face. The
  same `fonts.ready` handle earns its place twice over: a webfont swapping in
  changes the measured height of every copy block, so anything sized against
  those blocks (a scrim plate, a rail) is wrong until it re-measures.
- Lines are almost always right; words for a short punch line; characters
  approximately never, *"because it turns reading into waiting."*
- **One kinetic headline per act, at most.**

## What makes a `count` land (§7)

- **Ease out, hard.** A cubic ease-out, so most of the distance goes by in the
  first third and the last digits settle slowly. *"A linear count reads as a
  slot machine."*
- **1.2–1.8 s.** Under a second and the reader misses that it moved; past two
  and they are waiting for a number they have already guessed.
- **Fires at half visibility, once**, so the reader is looking at it when it
  starts, and it never re-runs on the way back up.
- **Pair it with the fade.** A counter inside a `data-sc-in` stack rises in
  with its label and starts ticking as it arrives — *"the same numbers static
  on the page read as a spreadsheet."*
- Write the target exactly as it should render, commas included; the engine
  strips them before parsing and applies `tabular-nums` so the layout does not
  jitter.

**A concept, fictional or pre-launch brand has no verified figures, so it has
no counters.** The device suits a SaaS or agency page and will look good in
the score table, *"which is exactly the trap: every number you could put in it
would be invented."* Decide this before designing an act around a number, not
after. Real brand, real stats, or a different device.

## Appendix: pattern vocabulary

Named patterns from taste-skill § 10, carried here so orchestrator, builder
and reviewer name the same thing. It is a **vocabulary, not a menu** — several
entries below are banned as directions elsewhere in the chain (glassmorphism,
holographic foil, carousels, gooey menus) and appear here only so a critique
can say which trope it is refusing.

- **Hero** — Asymmetric Split · Editorial Manifesto · Video/Media Mask ·
  Kinetic-Type · Curtain-Reveal · Scroll-Pinned.
- **Nav** — Dock Magnification · Magnetic Button (`data-sc-magnet`) · Gooey
  Menu · Dynamic Island · Contextual Radial · Floating Speed Dial · Mega Menu
  Reveal.
- **Layout** — Bento Grid · Masonry · Chroma Grid · Split-Screen Scroll ·
  Sticky-Stack Sections.
- **Cards** — Parallax Tilt Card (`data-sc-tilt`) · Spotlight Border Card
  (`data-sc-spotlight`) · Glassmorphism Panel · Holographic Foil ·
  Tinder Swipe Stack · Morphing Modal.
- **Scroll** — Sticky Scroll Stack · Horizontal Scroll Hijack (= `pan`) ·
  Locomotive / Sequence Scroll (= `scrub`) · Zoom Parallax · Scroll Progress
  Path · Liquid Swipe Transition.
- **Galleries** — Dome Gallery · Coverflow Carousel · Drag-to-Pan Grid ·
  Accordion Image Slider · Hover Image Trail · Glitch Effect Image.
- **Type** — Kinetic Marquee · **Text Mask Reveal** (massive type as a
  transparent window onto video — this is K2's letter-window) · Text Scramble
  · Circular Text Path · Gradient Stroke Animation · Kinetic Typography Grid.
- **Micro** — Particle Explosion Button · Liquid Pull-to-Refresh · Skeleton
  Shimmer · Directional Hover-Aware Button · Ripple Click · Animated SVG Line
  Drawing · Mesh Gradient Background · Lens Blur Depth.

Names alone are not permission. A pattern still has to clear the fingerprint
gate, the register, and `../motion.md` before it ships.

## Never restyle the engine's classes (AB06, 2026-09-03)

Theme the engine only through its six colour tokens and two fonts. A project rule on
`.sc-stage`, `.sc-copy`, `.sc-scrim` or any other `.sc-*` class silently wins over the
engine: the console then says `[scrollcraft] act "…" will not pin: its stage computes
position:relative` and every pinned act scrolls away, leaving its spacer as dead scroll.
Read the console for `[scrollcraft]` warnings before anything else in Step 5, and run
`scripts/scroll_verify.py` — a blind one-shot cannot see either. The engine is opt-in per
grammar (scrub, pin, pan); a page that keeps the chain's own single set-piece + shared
reveal does not need it.

and the project has UI files). By hand:

```bash

python ~/.agents/skills/design/scripts/motion/link_motion.py <project> --check
```

What it does, and why each step exists:

2. Adds `"gsap": "^3.15.0", "lenis": "^1.3.26"` to `dependencies` when absent.

   next `npm install <anything>` prunes them silently. With semver deps the links survive

   `file:../../AppData/Roaming/...`, a machine path that breaks every other machine and Vercel.

   the second was linked separately). Windowless (`CREATE_NO_WINDOW`).

   Never overwrites.

  The template registers 19 plugins, more than the architecture file's 14: it adds
  `CustomEase`, `CustomBounce`, `CustomWiggle`, `EasePack` and `Physics2DPlugin`.

  § The engine). Import it once, early: `import lenis from "./smooth-scroll.js"`.

490–724 px in V3g), and the Lenis options `autoRaf:false, anchors:true,
respectReducedMotion:false, lerp:.075, wheelMultiplier:.6`.

| Entry | gzip |
|---|---|
| template `gsap.js` (all 19 plugins) + Lenis | 115 kB |

page calls. It is the only file to edit, since nothing else imports gsap directly.
`performance.md` § 1 owns the budget.

## 4. Per project type

**Static HTML (the house prototypes, `tests/*/runs/*`).** Serve the project root over
http and give the page an import map. Verified headless (Chromium, 0 console errors,
0 4xx): SplitText with mask, pinned scrubbed ScrollTrigger, Lenis smoothing at house pace
(10 wheel notches = 720 px).

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/node_modules/lenis/dist/lenis.css">
<script type="importmap">
{ "imports": {
  "gsap": "/node_modules/gsap/index.js",
  "gsap/all": "/node_modules/gsap/all.js",
  "gsap/": "/node_modules/gsap/",
  "lenis": "/node_modules/lenis/dist/lenis.mjs"
} }
```

without `.js`. Paths are server-root-relative, so serve the folder that holds
`node_modules`. A page nested deeper (a board cell) uses `../../node_modules/...`.

first (`npx esbuild main.js --bundle --minify --format=esm --outfile=assets/app.js`).

into `.vite/deps`, serves `lenis.css` through `/@fs/` (200), and `vite build` bundles
3.15.0 from the link. In the entry: `import "lenis/dist/lenis.css"`.

`turbopack.root` (or `outputFileTracingRoot`) covers the target. Test `next build` once in a
real Next project before trusting the link there.

Do: link, never install · import only through `gsap.js` · one Lenis instance in
`smooth-scroll.js` · `lenis.on('scroll', ScrollTrigger.update)` · `gsap.ticker` drives Lenis ·
trim `gsap.js` before shipping · `npm list gsap lenis` as the check.

Never: `npm install gsap|lenis` · plugins installed separately · `registerPlugin` outside
`gsap.js` · a Lenis instance per component · `ScrollSmoother.create()` on a Lenis page (two
scroll owners) · JavaScript imports typed into PowerShell · `npm link --save`.

## 6. Full potential — what the tools are for

The API lives in the official skills (`gsap-core`, `gsap-scrolltrigger`, `gsap-timeline`,
`gsap-plugins`, `gsap-utils`, `gsap-performance`, `gsap-react`, `lenis`). What a
showcase-level page does with the API, and which plugin carries each move, is in
`showcase-floor.md`, read from 646 GSAP and Lenis showcase sites.

                 [--explain] [--json] [--root ROOT] [--dry-run]

select.py - pick the 2-4 catalogue entries a brief must be measured against.

Why this exists
---------------
r7 (2026-09-06/07) put the slugs straight into the builder prompt. The builders
read them, so the reference floor was satisfied, and `Skill(design-catalog)`
was still never invoked: the *selection* came out of the orchestrator's memory,
not out of the catalogue. Nothing could tell the difference afterwards.

This script is that difference. It scores every entry in index.json against the
brief's declared register / grammar / category / authority plus its free text,
prints a ranked list, and writes ONE `catalogue-select` row into the session
ledger naming the chosen slugs. design-gate.py's reference floor requires that
row before the first UI write, so a build cannot proceed on recalled references.

Deterministic. No model call anywhere in here.

    python scripts/catalogue/select.py --brief BRIEF.md [--k 4] [--wildcard]
                                       [--exclude slug,slug] [--explain] [--json]
                                       [--root DIR] [--dry-run]

options:
  -h, --help         show this help message and exit
  --brief BRIEF
  --k K
  --exclude EXCLUDE
  --wildcard         add one high-scoring entry from OUTSIDE the brief's
                     category - the catalogue IS the category, so a move it
                     does not contain has to come from somewhere else
  --explain
  --json
  --root ROOT        project root whose ledger gets the row
  --dry-run          rank, write no ledger row

usage: select.py [-h] --brief BRIEF [--k K] [--exclude EXCLUDE] [--wildcard]
                 [--explain] [--json] [--root ROOT] [--dry-run]

select.py - pick the 2-4 catalogue entries a brief must be measured against.

Why this exists
---------------
r7 (2026-09-06/07) put the slugs straight into the builder prompt. The builders
read them, so the reference floor was satisfied, and `Skill(design-catalog)`
was still never invoked: the *selection* came out of the orchestrator's memory,
not out of the catalogue. Nothing could tell the difference afterwards.

This script is that difference. It scores every entry in index.json against the
brief's declared register / grammar / category / authority plus its free text,
prints a ranked list, and writes ONE `catalogue-select` row into the session
ledger naming the chosen slugs. design-gate.py's reference floor requires that
row before the first UI write, so a build cannot proceed on recalled references.

Deterministic. No model call anywhere in here.

    python scripts/catalogue/select.py --brief BRIEF.md [--k 4] [--wildcard]
                                       [--exclude slug,slug] [--explain] [--json]
                                       [--root DIR] [--dry-run]

options:
  -h, --help         show this help message and exit
  --brief BRIEF
  --k K
  --exclude EXCLUDE
  --wildcard         add one high-scoring entry from OUTSIDE the brief's
                     category - the catalogue IS the category, so a move it
                     does not contain has to come from somewhere else
  --explain
  --json
  --root ROOT        project root whose ledger gets the row
  --dry-run          rank, write no ledger row

7	# Design fingerprint registry
8	
9	The fingerprint gate for scroll-choreographed Persuade/Experience builds. See
10	`.agents/skills/design/references/scroll/feel-and-fingerprint.md` § The
11	fingerprint gate for the rule: **a new build must differ from EVERY existing
12	row on at least 4 of the 6 dimension columns**, checked row by row, not
13	averaged across the table. If a planned build fails the gate, change the
14	plan, not this file — rewriting a row to make a new build fit is the one
15	thing that makes this registry worthless.
16	
17	Seeded 2026-09-03 with one row per existing example site in
18	`anti-slop-design/sites/`. These sites predate scroll-craft integration and
19	were not built against the nine-device kit or the eight named grammars — the
20	Grammar, Signature move and Register columns below are an honest read of what
21	each page actually does, mapped onto scroll-craft's vocabulary after the
22	fact, not a claim that they were built to it. Where a site has no bespoke
23	interaction beyond an ordinary reveal-on-scroll, the Signature move column
24	says `none` — that is a finding, not a gap in the audit.

36	## Reading this table before a new build
37	
38	Three grammar collisions already exist among these seven rows: Calyx,
39	Hyperborea and Vintergatan all read as chaptered editorial, and Vinterspelen
40	leans the same way with a gallery inflection. A new chaptered-editorial build
41	has to clear 3 more dimensions against **each** of those four rows
42	individually — nav treatment and hero device are the two that repeat across
43	them most (folio/edition-strip nav, type-in-photo or split-poster heroes), so
44	those are the columns most likely to collide again. Hōrai and Tidvatten share
45	grammar (filmic one-shot), a fixed minimal bar, a JS-parallax full-bleed
46	hero, and a bell-curve-scrub pinned set-piece as their signature move's
47	underlying mechanism — a third filmic one-shot build with a scrub-driven
48	pinned set-piece would need a genuinely different mechanism for the move, not
49	just different numbers on screen, to clear dimension 6 meaningfully even
50	though the gate counts it as free.
51	
52	`before-ai-slop.html` is not a build to avoid colliding with — it is the
53	negative reference. Any real build should differ from it on every dimension
54	by construction.
55	
56	## Alunix concept builds, rounds 1–7 (appended 2026-09-09)
57	
58	Twenty-nine rows, one per built `index.html` under `anti-slop-design/tests/alunix-*`.
59	Every column is derived from the cell's own files: the built HTML (nav markup, section
60	list, `data-sc-act` attributes, `:root` custom properties, font links), its `NOTES.md`
61	or `BRIEF.md`, and its desktop fold screenshot read as an image. Where a cell's own
62	files carry no evidence for a column, the cell says `?` rather than a guess — that is a
63	finding about the cell's documentation, not a licence to treat the dimension as free.
64	
65	Duplicates were excluded, not counted twice: `alunix-ab-r6/board/cells/*` are byte-identical
66	copies of the seven r6 runs, `alunix-ab-r7/board/cells/K1-1` and `K2-1` are byte-identical

68	`alunix-concepts-r5/reference/V3-baseline` is a byte-identical copy of `V3-chain`.

109	
110	Grammar has been spent hard. Chaptered editorial now has five rows here (r1 K4, r2 R2, R3,
111	R4, r4 M2) on top of the four seed rows, filmic one-shot has four (r6 A-K1, B-K1,
112	B-K1-nogate, r7 B-K1) on top of two seed rows, and typographic poster has five (r1 K3, r2
113	R6, r6 A-K2 and B-K2, r7 B-K2). Continuous world is a five-row family (M1, V1, V2, V3,
114	V3b) that also shares nav treatment and close pattern by construction, because every r5
115	variant inherited M1's chrome and its two closing objects; those five rows clear the gate
116	against each other only on hero device, act shape and signature move, which is exactly 3
117	of the 5 non-free dimensions, the bare minimum. A sixth build in that family would have
118	nowhere left to differ.
119	
120	Two nav patterns repeat across rounds and should be treated as used up: the thin
121	scrolling top row with wordmark and contact (M1, V1, V2, V3, V3b) and the fixed minimal
122	bar with logo left and contact right that darkens or lightens per ground (r6 A-K1, B-K1,
123	B-K1-nogate, r7 B-K1). Two hero devices likewise: the full-bleed blue-hour photograph
124	with a light-serif headline in the water (four rows) and the crushed poster wordmark with
125	the example screenshots showing through or beside the letters (four rows). The r7 rows
126	record their own shared dimensions honestly — each clears the gate at exactly 4 of 6
127	against its r6 predecessor, with grammar and nav knowingly shared — so a v3 of either
128	concept cannot reuse the hero device, the act shape or the close as well.
129	
130	Ten rows carried `?` in Register when the r1–r7 block was first appended: r2 R3, R4 and
131	R5, the r3 build, r4 M1 and M2, and r5 V1, V2, V3 and V3b. Those cells' own files name
132	grammar, world and palette but never a register from the six-name vocabulary, and no
133	sibling file names it for them either. On 2026-09-09 the column was filled for all ten by
134	reading each cell's `index.html` directly (and, for the r3 build and r4 M2, its 1440 fold
135	as pixels) against `design/SKILL.md`'s register table and its "what varies with register"
136	markers: face, grain, buttons versus typeset links, ground and subject. Every one of the
137	ten reads as **modern clean** — one lineage, sans display with mono as register only, no
138	serif and no grain anywhere, one blue accent, ledgers over cards, and a precision subject
139	— which is the same read the registry already recorded for r1 K1, K2, K5, K6 and r2 R1
140	and R2. Each cell states the file it was derived from, so the derivation is auditable and
141	declared as post-hoc, exactly like the seven seed rows above.

# Design fingerprint registry

The fingerprint gate for scroll-choreographed Persuade/Experience builds. See
`.agents/skills/design/references/scroll/feel-and-fingerprint.md` § The
fingerprint gate for the rule: **a new build must differ from EVERY existing
row on at least 4 of the 6 dimension columns**, checked row by row, not
averaged across the table. If a planned build fails the gate, change the
plan, not this file — rewriting a row to make a new build fit is the one
thing that makes this registry worthless.

Seeded 2026-09-03 with one row per existing example site in
`anti-slop-design/sites/`. These sites predate scroll-craft integration and
were not built against the nine-device kit or the eight named grammars — the
Grammar, Signature move and Register columns below are an honest read of what
each page actually does, mapped onto scroll-craft's vocabulary after the
fact, not a claim that they were built to it. Where a site has no bespoke
interaction beyond an ordinary reveal-on-scroll, the Signature move column
says `none` — that is a finding, not a gap in the audit.

| Build | Grammar | Nav treatment | Hero device | Act-sequence shape | Close pattern | Signature move | Register | World / palette | Path |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Calyx | Chaptered editorial | Static (non-sticky) border-b header, 3-col grid: edition kicker · centred wordmark · two text anchors | Full-bleed botanical photo, gradient scrim, headline lead-corner bottom-left, kicker+copy trail-corner bottom-right | ~8 sections: hero > manifesto/quote > duo photo pair > index/commission ledger (`.01`–`.04`) > immersion photo break > testimonial ledger > commission CTA | Dark-inverted section, mailto set as huge italic display type with arrow; 4-col colophon footer | none — plain IntersectionObserver fade/rise reveal and ordinary image-hover scale only | Editorial print | Cardo (display) + PT Mono (kicker); cream / bone / moss / ink / rust | `anti-slop-design/sites/calyx.html` |
| Hōrai | Filmic one-shot | Fixed bar, transparent → dark-blurred on scroll; wordmark + "RESERVATIONS" button | Full-bleed JS-parallax photo, giant wordmark, JP kicker, two-column lede | ~7 sections: hero > the house (word-lit lede) > pinned scroll-scrubbed quote chapter > set menus (3 numbered courses) > photo spread > the room (parallax) > reservations CTA | Dark section, "book.horai.se" as huge typeset link + mailto, address, 3-col colophon | Pinned quote set-piece: kicker + gold rules + JP glyphs + blockquote scrub in/out on a bell-curve proximity-to-viewport-center function, independent per-element stagger (blur, scale, translate, tracking), `?preview=quote` hook | Cinematic dark | Cinzel + Vollkorn + Noto Serif JP; paper / walnut / lacquer / jade | `anti-slop-design/sites/horai.html` |

## Reading this table before a new build

Three grammar collisions already exist among these seven rows: Calyx,
Hyperborea and Vintergatan all read as chaptered editorial, and Vinterspelen
leans the same way with a gallery inflection. A new chaptered-editorial build
has to clear 3 more dimensions against **each** of those four rows
individually — nav treatment and hero device are the two that repeat across
them most (folio/edition-strip nav, type-in-photo or split-poster heroes), so
those are the columns most likely to collide again. Hōrai and Tidvatten share
grammar (filmic one-shot), a fixed minimal bar, a JS-parallax full-bleed
hero, and a bell-curve-scrub pinned set-piece as their signature move's
underlying mechanism — a third filmic one-shot build with a scrub-driven
pinned set-piece would need a genuinely different mechanism for the move, not
just different numbers on screen, to clear dimension 6 meaningfully even
though the gate counts it as free.

`before-ai-slop.html` is not a build to avoid colliding with — it is the
negative reference. Any real build should differ from it on every dimension
by construction.

## Alunix concept builds, rounds 1–7 (appended 2026-09-09)

Twenty-nine rows, one per built `index.html` under `anti-slop-design/tests/alunix-*`.
Every column is derived from the cell's own files: the built HTML (nav markup, section
list, `data-sc-act` attributes, `:root` custom properties, font links), its `NOTES.md`
or `BRIEF.md`, and its desktop fold screenshot read as an image. Where a cell's own
files carry no evidence for a column, the cell says `?` rather than a guess — that is a
finding about the cell's documentation, not a licence to treat the dimension as free.

Duplicates were excluded, not counted twice: `alunix-ab-r6/board/cells/*` are byte-identical
copies of the seven r6 runs, `alunix-ab-r7/board/cells/K1-1` and `K2-1` are byte-identical

Rounds 1–2 and 6 predate scroll-craft integration in those cells (no `data-sc-*` in the
markup); their act shapes are hand-rolled. Rounds 3–5 and 7 run the engine. In r6 and r7,
arm A is the Claude-native control (Anthropic's `frontend-design` system prompt, no skills,
no hooks) and arm B is this chain; `B-K1-nogate` is the r6 chain run where the gate never
fired, kept as its own row because it is a separate build.

### What these rows share, and what the next Alunix build has to avoid

Grammar has been spent hard. Chaptered editorial now has five rows here (r1 K4, r2 R2, R3,
R4, r4 M2) on top of the four seed rows, filmic one-shot has four (r6 A-K1, B-K1,
B-K1-nogate, r7 B-K1) on top of two seed rows, and typographic poster has five (r1 K3, r2
R6, r6 A-K2 and B-K2, r7 B-K2). Continuous world is a five-row family (M1, V1, V2, V3,
V3b) that also shares nav treatment and close pattern by construction, because every r5
variant inherited M1's chrome and its two closing objects; those five rows clear the gate
against each other only on hero device, act shape and signature move, which is exactly 3
of the 5 non-free dimensions, the bare minimum. A sixth build in that family would have
nowhere left to differ.

Two nav patterns repeat across rounds and should be treated as used up: the thin
scrolling top row with wordmark and contact (M1, V1, V2, V3, V3b) and the fixed minimal
bar with logo left and contact right that darkens or lightens per ground (r6 A-K1, B-K1,
B-K1-nogate, r7 B-K1). Two hero devices likewise: the full-bleed blue-hour photograph
with a light-serif headline in the water (four rows) and the crushed poster wordmark with
the example screenshots showing through or beside the letters (four rows). The r7 rows
record their own shared dimensions honestly — each clears the gate at exactly 4 of 6
against its r6 predecessor, with grammar and nav knowingly shared — so a v3 of either
concept cannot reuse the hero device, the act shape or the close as well.

Ten rows carried `?` in Register when the r1–r7 block was first appended: r2 R3, R4 and
R5, the r3 build, r4 M1 and M2, and r5 V1, V2, V3 and V3b. Those cells' own files name
grammar, world and palette but never a register from the six-name vocabulary, and no
sibling file names it for them either. On 2026-09-09 the column was filled for all ten by
reading each cell's `index.html` directly (and, for the r3 build and r4 M2, its 1440 fold
as pixels) against `design/SKILL.md`'s register table and its "what varies with register"
markers: face, grain, buttons versus typeset links, ground and subject. Every one of the
ten reads as **modern clean** — one lineage, sans display with mono as register only, no
serif and no grain anywhere, one blue accent, ledgers over cards, and a precision subject
— which is the same read the registry already recorded for r1 K1, K2, K5, K6 and r2 R1
and R2. Each cell states the file it was derived from, so the derivation is auditable and
declared as post-hoc, exactly like the seven seed rows above.

ALUNIX
kontakt@alunix.se
Er hemsida är nutidens visitkort
Alunix. Digital byrå. Design, utveckling, system. Boka ett möte: kontakt@alunix.se.
Alunix
Digital byrå
Design
Utveckling
System
Boka ett möte
Det första intrycket är digitalt.
Vi hjälper er att synas på rätt sätt.
Vi hjälper er att synas på rätt sätt.
Vår process:
Från samtal till lanserad sida.
Webbdesign, design och system. Allt på ett ställe.
01
Uppstart
Vi börjar med ett samtal om er verksamhet samt vad ni vill att sidan ska göra för er. Utifrån det skapar vi ett initialt underlag som ni rättar innan det går till ritbordet.
02
Planering
Vi ritar strukturen som en skiss innan vi formger något. Där ser ni vilka sidor som behövs och vad varje sida ska få besökaren att göra, mobilen först.
03
Design
När strukturen står formger vi sidan efter er verksamhet. Förslaget lägger vi på en testadress, där ni ser det på er egen telefon och säger till innan det går till bygge.
04
Utveckling
Vi bygger sidan i kod från grunden, utan färdig mall, så att den laddar snabbt. Texter och bilder ändrar ni själva, och vill ni lägga till mer bygger ni vidare på det vi lämnat.
05
Innehåll
Ni behöver inte ha något färdigt. Det ni har bearbetar vi, bygger vidare på och kompletterar där något saknas. Texten skriver vi åt er, om ni inte vill ha er egen.
06
Lansering
Innan sidan publiceras går vi igenom varje länk, formulär och bild. Vi testar den med tangentbord och skärmläsare, på telefon och på dator, och visar er hur ni ändrar innehållet själva.
07
Förvaltning
Vi finns kvar efter lansering. Nya sidor och ändringar går samma väg som bygget, så ni ser dem på testadressen innan era kunder gör det. Har ni en fråga mejlar ni oss på kontakt@alunix.se.
Exempelcase
Calyx
Florist, Stockholm
Hōrai
Restaurang, Asian Fusion
Calyx
Florist, Stockholm
Öppna Calyx i full storlek
01 / 05
Sidan öppnar som ett omslag
Blommor väljs med ögonen innan någon läser ett pris. Därför fick fotot hela första skärmen, så att det första besökaren möter är arbetet och inte en knapp. Omslaget ger också ateljén ett skäl att byta bild varje säsong, och då känns sidan ny utan att byggas om.
En serif får bära allt
Rubriker, brödtext och namn står i samma serif, bara etiketterna i skrivmaskinsstil, så sidan läses som en trycksak. Ett andra rubriktypsnitt hade gett mer kontrast, men också dragit sidan mot reklam. Ateljén levererar till hotell och restauranger som själva lägger pengar på sitt tryck, och de ser skillnaden.
Varje bild är ett uppdrag
